raised: The submitters of 217 (and the earlier 7) say discrimination that members experience within A.A. is a safety issue that must be addressed, and that discrimination against marginalized communities goes against Traditions One, Three and Five.

Item 100 asks that all work on the transgender pamphlet stop; its text in the grid gives no reason. Item 69 asks to leave “Eskimo” in the Big Book and not to read present-day meanings into 1939 wording; it also asks for changes to the stories, saying stories by transgender members are not needed and suggesting fewer stories by gay members.
Item 214 asks for a clarification: that the 1986 and 1987 guidance on Double-Trouble groups in directories also applies to the Meeting Guide app run by A.A. World Services.

considerations.text: In 2026 the trustees' Literature Committee noted that service material is under the purview of A.A. World Services (AAWS) and General Service Office staff, not the General Service Conference. The safety-statement item (217) and the Meeting Guide item (214) were sent to AAWS.
considerations.cite: 2026 Final Report p. 106; proposal grid for the 77th Conference (Oct. 1, 2026)

considerations.text: Describing literature and service material on accessibility, the Service Manual says there are no special alcoholics, but there are alcoholics who face barriers to receiving the A.A. message, and general service looks for ways to minimize and ultimately remove those barriers.

The General Service Office's new-group guidance quotes the long form of Tradition Three: membership ought to include all who suffer from alcoholism, and any two or three alcoholics may call themselves a group if, as a group, they have no other affiliation. The office lists groups, not meetings, and says a listing is not an endorsement.
The 1986–87 actions were written about A.A. directories. Meeting Guide instead relays meeting listings that more than 500 A.A. service entities supply voluntarily and keep full control of.

questions: What does our group do now when a member feels unsafe or unwelcome, and what A.A. material has helped?
Should A.A.'s safety service material address discrimination by name? What might be gained or lost either way?
Pamphlets written for particular groups of alcoholics: in our group's experience, do they help newcomers identify, or do they set people apart?
How should guidance written for printed group directories in 1986–87 apply to an app where local A.A. service entities supply the meeting listings?
themes.watch: Decisions on 100 (trustees' Literature Committee) and on 214 and 217 (A.A. World Services board) around the fall board meetings (Oct 29–Nov 2, 2026); the transgender pamphlet's progress report or draft at the 2027 Conference; and safety video progress.

asks.protect: make a text or practice harder to change, or keep it as it is
asks.restore: undo a past change and bring back earlier wording or practice
asks.change: amend existing wording, policy or practice
asks.create: make something new (literature, video, body, tool, policy that did not exist)
asks.procedure: change how the Conference or the board decides things
asks.study: ask for a review, study, report, audit or information

items.title: Article 12 protection: 164 pages, Doctor's Opinion, Dr. Bob's Nightmare
items.summary: Asks, on behalf of two districts in Area 25, that Charter Article 12 be amended so The Doctor's Opinion, the first 164 pages and Dr. Bob's Nightmare could not be revised or modernized without the Fellowship-wide group consent Article 12 itself requires; typo and formatting fixes would stay allowed.

items.conf_reason: Report and Charter reviews proposed Charter changes (Service Manual p. 47); it took up 2025 requests to expand Article Three (2025 Final Report p. 51).
items.note: Article 12 (the General Warranties) is protected by Article 3's last sentence and the 1955 Resolution: written consent of three-quarters of responding groups after at least six months (Service Manual pp. 124, 128). So amending Article 12, as asked here, would itself need that consent.
items.differs: Targets Article 12 rather than Article 3 (as in #57, #72 and #197); spells out rewriting and modernizing as barred; like #158 it exempts typographical and formatting fixes.

items.title: Do not change the Big Book's first 164 pages in any way
items.summary: Asks, for a group, that the first 164 pages of the Big Book not be changed in any way. It names no mechanism, such as a Charter amendment or an Advisory Action.

responds_to.what: Action that the first 164 pages and other core parts remain as is

items.conf_reason: Filed with the Charter items; Report and Charter received 2025 requests to protect co-founders' writings (2025 Final Report p. 89; Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: A 1995 action says the first 164 pages, Preface, Forewords, “The Doctor's Opinion,” “Doctor Bob's Nightmare” and Appendices remain as is (p2773). In 2026 the Conference replaced “Eskimo” in Chapter 7, “Working With Others” (p3139).
items.differs: Nearly the same as #30 and #118; like them it names no mechanism, unlike #114 or the Charter items such as #57 and #72, which require three-quarters written group consent.

items.title: Committee recommendations not on the agenda wait for next year
items.summary: Proposes that, starting with the 77th Conference, a Conference committee recommendation on a subject that was not on the agenda would not be voted on that year but would go automatically onto the next Conference's agenda.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: A 1986 action sends weighty, long-term or costly matters raised in the Conference's final hours to the next year's committee (p3457); a 1963 Agenda action offers items not on the current agenda to the next year's committee (p32).
items.differs: Nearly the same as #117. Covers only committee recommendations that were not on the agenda; #149 covers floor motions and #39 and #178 cover both.

items.title: Hold floor proposals changing the first 164 pages to next Conference
items.summary: Asks that any floor proposal that would change anything in the Big Book's first 164 pages be held over to the next General Service Conference instead of being decided that year.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: Under Conference rules, tabling postpones discussion only to later in the same Conference (Service Manual p. 174). In 2026 the Chapter 7 “Eskimo” change came from the Literature Committee (p3139) and the Twelve and Twelve change from a floor action (p3135).
items.differs: Narrower than #149 (all floor motions): only floor proposals touching the first 164 pages. #208 bars floor votes on Big Book changes; #170 seeks a similar wait for committee recommendations.
items.quote: should be tabled until the next GSC

items.title: New floor and committee matters go to next year's agenda unless three-fourths agree
items.summary: Proposes that committee recommendations and floor actions on new policy, structural, financial, governance or literature matters not previously handled through the Conference committee process go to next year's Conference as proposed agenda items, unless a three-fourths vote finds them urgent and essential to the structure's duties; lists exceptions and exclusions.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: Committee recommendations and floor actions need a two-thirds vote (Service Manual p. 175). A 1986 action sends weighty or costly matters raised late to the next year's committee (p3457). A 1953 rule required three-quarters of members present for matters gravely affecting A.A. (p3157).
items.differs: Longer form of #178, adding a three-fourths exception vote and lists of qualifying and excluded matters; #19 and #117 offer no exception route.

items.title: Significant changes should come through the yearly agenda item process
items.summary: Asks the Conference to recommend that any significant proposed change to A.A. literature, Conference policy or Fellowship-wide matters come through the regular yearly proposed agenda item process.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 agenda-routing actions came from it (p3462).
items.note: The Service Manual lists who may suggest agenda items (members, groups, delegates, area assemblies, trustees, directors and staff) and says every item follows the same path through the Conference coordinator and trustees' committees (pp. 43, 171).
items.differs: Less specific than #19, #39 and #117: asks that significant proposals use the yearly submission process but does not say what happens to items raised during Conference week.

items.title: Substantive matters must start as agenda items or floor actions
items.summary: Proposes a policy that every substantive matter needing Conference approval start either as a properly submitted agenda item or as a properly introduced floor action during the Conference.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: A matter within a committee's scope ought first to go through that committee, but floor actions may come any time except sharing sessions (Service Manual p. 174). A 1957 action lets a delegate whose proposal is withheld raise it on the floor (p3189).
items.differs: Unlike #19, #117 and #149, it keeps floor actions as an accepted starting point; it lists only agenda items and floor actions as the two routes.

items.title: Committee recommendations not on the original agenda wait for next year
items.summary: Proposes that, from the 77th Conference on, any committee recommendation on a matter not on the original agenda would not be voted on that year and would be placed automatically on the next year's agenda.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: Under current rules, the full Conference is not obliged to accept a committee's report and decides each matter in general session (Service Manual p. 42). A 1986 action sends weighty matters raised late to the next year's committee (p3457).
items.differs: Almost the same as #19; it adds “original” before agenda and says such items “shall not be voted on that year”.

items.title: Floor motions passed at the Conference go to a committee, then wait a year
items.summary: Proposes that a floor motion passed during the Conference be sent to the matching committee; if the committee approves it, it would go on the next year's agenda rather than take effect that year.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: Today a floor action's maker gets two minutes, the Conference may decline to consider it, and it needs a two-thirds vote (Service Manual pp. 174-175). In 2025 there were 12 floor actions: one passed, nine declined, two recommitted (2025 Final Report p. 5).
items.differs: Parallel to #172, which covers committee motions. Unlike #19 and #117, a passed floor motion first goes to a committee and only then to the next year's agenda.

items.title: Committees need a proposed agenda item before introducing changes
items.summary: Proposes that committees in the general service structure could not bring changes to literature, policies, procedures or the makeup and duties of the service structure unless first submitted as a proposed agenda item, with background, for review before the annual Conference.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); in 2026 it proposed a one-year lead time for procedure changes (2026 Final Report p. 42).
items.note: In 2026 a Policy/Admissions recommendation that changes beyond editorial to the “How the Conference Operates” document be discussed a year before use fell short of two-thirds (2026 Final Report p. 42).
items.differs: Wider than #19 and #117: covers any committee in the service structure and changes to literature, policy, procedures and structure, requiring review before the Conference rather than during it.

items.title: Floor motions passed at the Conference go to a committee, then wait a year
items.summary: Proposes that a floor motion passed during the Conference be sent to the matching committee; if the committee approves it, it would go on the next year's agenda rather than take effect that year.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: Today a floor action's maker gets two minutes, the Conference may decline to consider it, and it needs a two-thirds vote (Service Manual pp. 174-175). In 2025 there were 12 floor actions: one passed, nine declined, two recommitted (2025 Final Report p. 5).

items.title: Committee motions passed at the Conference wait until the next year
items.summary: Proposes that motions coming out of Conference committees and passed during the Conference week be placed on the following year's agenda and not take effect in the current year.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: A committee recommendation is presented in the committee report, automatically seconded and needs a two-thirds vote (Service Manual p. 175); approved Advisory Actions go to the General Service Board, which affirms them and sends them on for implementation (p. 43).
items.differs: Parallel to #149 (floor motions); unlike #19 and #117 it does not limit itself to items that were off the agenda.

items.title: New floor and committee matters go to next year's agenda
items.summary: Asks the Conference to consider a process under which substantive committee recommendations and floor actions raising new policy, structural, financial, governance or literature matters, not already considered through the regular committee process, become proposed agenda items for the following year's Conference instead of being decided that week.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 practice for late floor matters came from Policy/Admissions (p3457).
items.note: A 1986 action sends weighty, long-term or costly matters raised in the final hours to the next year's committee (p3457). A 2026 recommendation that committees may defer items to a later Conference was committed to the General Service Board (2026 Final Report p. 42).
items.differs: Shorter form of #39, without its three-fourths exception route. Broader than #45, which applies the next-year referral only to committee recommendations that may change the founders' writings (the Big Book's first 164 pages).

items.title: Guidelines for floor actions that would override past Advisory Actions
items.summary: Asks the Conference to set guidelines for floor actions that would change, replace or conflict with an earlier Advisory Action, including a way for the Fellowship to give informed input through the service structure before final action.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and set the 1986 guidance on late floor actions (p3455, p3457).
items.note: Floor actions need a two-thirds vote to pass, and the Conference may first vote, also by two-thirds, to decline to consider one (Service Manual p. 175). A 1986 action sends weighty matters raised late in the week to the next year's committee (p3457).
items.differs: Unlike #19, #117 and #149, which send late matters to the next year, it asks for guidelines on floor actions that would change an earlier Advisory Action, with Fellowship input first.

items.title: Change the Conference's floor action process (no details given)
items.summary: Proposes a change to how floor actions work at the General Service Conference; the grid wording does not say what the change would be.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and brought a 2021 floor-procedure proposal (2021 Final Report p. 73).
items.note: In 2021 a proposal letting a simple majority decide whether to hear floor actions won a majority but not two-thirds (2021 Final Report p. 73); in 2022 trustees took no action on a request to change floor-action procedures (2022 Final Report p. 40).
items.differs: Gives no details; the other floor-procedure items (for example #19, #149 and #178) say what they would change.

items.title: Big Book changes from committees go to groups first as agenda items
items.summary: Proposes that Conference committee recommendations that may change the founders' writings (it names the Big Book's first 164 pages) be written as proposed agenda items, approved by the Conference and sent to the groups for the next year's Conference, to keep A.A.'s “upside-down triangle” structure.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and took up voting rules for co-founders' writings in 2025 (2025 Final Report p. 90).
items.note: The 1995 Conference said the first 164 pages and other core sections stay as they are (p2773); in 2026 it replaced one word in Chapter 7 through a Literature committee recommendation (p3139; 2026 Final Report p. 40).

items.title: Never change the Big Book; revise only the Plain Language Big Book

items.title: Three-quarters vote to change core Big Book and Twelve and Twelve text

items.conf_reason: A 2025 super-majority request for founders' literature went to Policy/Admissions, which examines Conference policy (2025 Final Report p. 90; Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: A 2024 floor action seeking a 75% vote to change founders' writings was recommitted to trustees (2024 Final Report pp. 52-53); in 2025 Policy/Admissions took no action on a super-majority request, noting it may be preemptive before defining co-founders' writings (2025 Final Report pp. 47-48).
items.differs: Unlike #87 (two-thirds after Fellowship-wide consideration), it asks for three-quarters of Conference voting members, and lists the Forewords, The Doctor's Opinion and Dr. Bob's Nightmare.

items.title: Two-year wait before votes on changing Bill W.'s writings
items.summary: Asks that Conference policy require a two-year waiting period before any vote to change Bill W.'s writings in Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions and in the Big Book (pages xxv-164).
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and discussed a two-year process for co-founders' writings in 2025 (2025 Final Report p. 48).
items.note: In 2025 Policy/Admissions noted a two-year process might be considered before votes on changing co-founders' writings (2025 Final Report p. 48); in 2026 the trustees' General Service Conference Committee routed that consideration to the trustees' Literature Committee chair (2026 Final Report p. 83).
items.differs: Like #86 and #167 it sets a two-year period; those name Big Book page ranges and the proposed agenda item process, while this one covers Bill W.'s writings in both books.

items.title: Do not change the Big Book's first 164 pages in any way
items.summary: Asks, for a group in Florida, that the first 164 pages of the Big Book not be changed in any way. It names no mechanism, such as a Charter amendment or an Advisory Action.

responds_to.what: Restates the 1995 action that the first 164 pages remain as is

items.conf_reason: A guess: the General Service Office (GSO) filed it with the Fellowship-review items, and in 2025 the trustees' General Service Conference Committee sent a similar founders'-literature request to Policy and Admissions (2025 Final Report p. 90). #30 and #204, filed with the Charter items, are guessed as Report and Charter.
items.note: The 1995 Conference said the first 164 pages, Preface, Forewords, “The Doctor's Opinion,” “Doctor Bob's Nightmare” and Appendices remain as is (p2773). In 2026 the Conference replaced one word in Chapter 7 (p3139).

items.title: Area input before votes on Big Book or Twelve and Twelve changes
items.summary: Asks that delegates hear from their areas before discussing or voting on changes to the Big Book's first 164 pages, Preface, Forewords, “The Doctor's Opinion,” “Dr. Bob's Nightmare” and Appendices, or to any Twelve and Twelve text, so such changes could not come only from committees or floor actions.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and took up voting rules for co-founders' writings in 2025 (2025 Final Report p. 90).
items.note: The Charter leaves delegates free to decide which questions to take to the group level (Article 3, Service Manual p. 124). In 2026 the Twelve and Twelve “Eskimo” change came from a floor action (p3135), the Big Book one from the Literature committee (p3139).
items.differs: Like #211 it has delegates hear from their areas first, but it also covers the Twelve and Twelve and other Big Book sections, and says such changes cannot come only from committees or floor actions.

items.title: Hold any Big Book changes until A.A. as a whole weighs in
items.summary: Moves, on behalf of a group, to put off any change to the Big Book until the collective conscience of A.A. as a whole is heard, saying the change in question was not on the agenda or raised at district level.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and took up voting rules for co-founders' writings in 2025 (2025 Final Report p. 90).
items.note: In 2026 the Conference replaced one word in Big Book Chapter 7 (p3139), approved the Fifth Edition (p3138) and declined to consider a floor action to pause its printing until there was more consensus on changing founders' writings (2026 Final Report p. 42).
items.differs: Like #208 it asks that the groups be heard before any Big Book change, but it sets out no procedure; it says the change it objects to was not on the agenda.

items.title: Policy to inform groups before changes to the first 164 pages
items.summary: Asks the Conference to consider a policy that the Fellowship be told about any proposed change to the first 164 pages of the Big Book, given background, and allowed time for groups to reach and report an informed group conscience before the change is approved or put into effect.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and took up voting rules for co-founders' writings in 2025 (2025 Final Report p. 90).
items.note: In 2024 a Conference committee reviewing Fellowship input on changes to founders' writings concluded current procedures let each Conference consider such proposals, “negating the need for a mandated policy” (2024 Final Report p. 43).
items.differs: Uses nearly the same safeguard wording as #124 (which also restores “Eskimo”) and the change policy in #161 (which also defines founders' writings); this one covers only changes to the first 164 pages.

items.title: Two-year Fellowship review before changing core Big Book pages (Fourth Edition)

items.differs: Nearly identical to #86; this version names the Fourth Edition and lists the covered sections in an asterisk footnote rather than in parentheses.

items.title: Written editorial policy for Big Book and Twelve and Twelve revisions
items.summary: Asks for a written, published editorial policy that would govern any substantive editorial revisions to the Big Book (Alcoholics Anonymous) and to Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions.

In 2014 a proposal to limit “editorial changes” in the earlier version to factual and mechanical fixes went back to that board (p3010).

items.title: Two-thirds requirement for Fellowship items among all agenda items
items.summary: Asks the General Service Board to give priority to proposed agenda items (PAIs) from the Fellowship, ensuring at least 67% of items considered come from the Fellowship and no more than 33% from trustees or staff of the two operating corporations, matching the Conference's own makeup.

items.title: Two-thirds goal for Fellowship items among new Final Agenda items
items.summary: Proposes that proposed agenda items (PAIs) sent in directly by the Fellowship make up a large share of the new items on each Conference's Final Agenda, with at least two-thirds as the target.

items.title: Let A.A. outside U.S./Canada take part in founders' writings changes
items.summary: Asks for a way for individuals, groups and other bodies outside the U.S./Canada service structure to take part when changes are proposed to any writings of A.A.'s founders dating from before 1971.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); Report and Charter could also take it, since Charter Article 2 covers other countries.
items.note: Charter Article 2: other countries' Conferences rely on the Steps and Traditions the U.S./Canada Conference protects; only matters seriously affecting worldwide needs are considered jointly (Service Manual p. 124). In 2025 the board was asked to classify pre-1971 A.A. World Services and Grapevine literature (p4819).
items.differs: Unlike the freezes in #42, #53 and #173, it asks for a way for A.A. outside the U.S./Canada structure to take part, and dates the writings as pre-1971.

items.title: Create a delegate area for online-only groups
items.summary: Asks the Conference to recommend that the General Service Board take the structural steps needed to set up a new area in the U.S./Canada structure for A.A. groups that meet only online and are not tied to an existing area.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions reviews requests to create additional delegate areas (Service Manual p. 47) and discussed an online-groups area in 2024.

items.title: Create a virtual area with its own assemblies, districts and delegate

items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions reviews requests to create additional delegate areas (Service Manual p. 47).

items.title: Reaffirm the Charter's description of who makes up area assemblies
items.summary: Asks the Conference to reaffirm Article 5 of the current Conference Charter, which says area assemblies consist of the elected general service representatives (GSRs) of participating groups, district committee members and area committee officers in each U.S. and Canadian delegate area.

responds_to.what: reaffirm the Charter Article 5 wording on who makes up area assemblies

items.title: Merge four outreach committees into one district and intergroup committee

items.note: Corrections and Treatment committees came from splitting one Institutions committee in 1977 (p3403). In 2026 Policy/Admissions took no action on ideas to give committees similar item counts regardless of topic or to add a Conference digital committee (2026 Final Report pp. 49–50).

items.title: Hold the General Service Conference online every other year
