items.summary: Asks that the 77th Conference (2027) hold a broad session on rebuilding the General Service Board's Reserve Fund.
items.conf_reason: Agenda considers workshop and presentation topics (Service Manual p. 46); the 2026 Finance committee asked Agenda to weigh a Reserve Fund session.
items.note: The Reserve Fund held 6.2 months of expenses in late 2025, below its nine-to-12-month target (2026 Final Report p. 14). The trustees' Finance committee favored a session on rebuilding it (p. 78); the Conference Finance committee asked Agenda to consider a 2027 workshop (p. 46).
items.differs: #133, #134 and #181 would set Reserve Fund minimums or replenishment rules and #179 would limit use of its income; this one asks only for a Conference session.

items.title: Workshop topic: what “right size” means at each service level
items.summary: Proposes, as a workshop, panel or presentation topic for 2027 and later Conferences and the board, a discussion of what A.A. means by “right size” when applied to districts, areas, regions, the Conference and the boards.
items.conf_reason: Agenda reviews proposed Conference themes, workshops and presentation/discussion topics (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: The 2026 Conference already chose the 2027 theme, presentation topics and workshop topic (p771, p772, p776). The Agenda committee reviews proposed themes and topics for later years (Service Manual p. 46).

items.title: Give Conference committees a formal role in setting their agenda
items.summary: Asks the Conference to change how its agenda is set so that Conference committees have a formal part in choosing their own agenda items, instead of the General Service Board deciding alone.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47) and handled a 2026 recommendation on selecting proposals (2026 Final Report p. 42); Agenda also fits.
items.note: Proposals go from General Service Office staff to a trustees' committee, which may refer them to a Conference committee (Service Manual p. 171). The 2026 Conference referred to the board a recommendation for joint committee votes on proposals (2026 Final Report p. 42).
items.differs: #63 and #98 reserve a share of agenda items for Fellowship proposals; this one gives committees a formal role in choosing items, like 76th grid items 34 and 85 (not forwarded).

items.title: Double the regions and enlarge the General Service Board
items.summary: Proposes enlarging the General Service Board: split the 8 regions into 16, which the text counts as raising alcoholic (Class B) trustees from 8 to 16, and raise nonalcoholic (Class A) trustees from 7 to 11, for a two-to-one board of 22 Class B and 11 Class A.
items.conf_reason: The 1966 board restructuring (p4910) and regional boundary guidelines (p5284) are Trustees committee actions; it also helps nominate regional trustees (Service Manual p. 48).
items.note: The board has 7 Class A and 14 Class B trustees, 8 of them regional trustees (six U.S., two Canada) (Service Manual pp. 52-53), a makeup set in 1966 (p4910, p4911). A similar 2025 idea (76th grid item 109) was not forwarded.

items.title: Create a third corporate board for A.A. social media
items.summary: Proposes a third corporation, beside A.A. World Services and AA Grapevine, with its own board to run A.A.'s social media (working name AADigitalMedia.Org). Says the idea was sent last year without trustee action and links it to a committee-reorganization proposal on Conference workload.
items.conf_reason: Board reorganization matters, such as the 2022 procedure (p5581), went to the Trustees committee; Public Information covers social media (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: The board now works through two operating corporations, A.A. World Services and AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 64), and the General Service Office's Communication Services oversees the social media channels (p. 74). The 2025 version, titled AASocialMedia.Org (76th grid item 40), was not forwarded.
items.differs: #103 merges four Conference committees but leaves digital media out; this one would move social media to a separate corporation.

items.title: Study an anonymous e-mail channel between members and the General Service Office
items.summary: Asks the Conference to have the General Service Board study and report on the feasibility, cost and funding of a voluntary, anonymous e-mail-style system that lets individual members receive news on major Fellowship matters and send advisory input to the General Service Office (GSO) and the service structure.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); no committee's scope names member communication tools.
items.note: A board working group of delegates, a staff member, a director and trustees reported on board-to-Conference communication in 2026; its ideas included an app with notifications to centralize communications (2026 Final Report pp. 10-11).
items.differs: #176 would add a similar two-way member channel to the new contributions platform; this one asks the board first to study a separate e-mail-type system.

items.title: Publish all literature in English, Spanish and French together
items.summary: Proposes that whenever an approved piece of A.A. literature is revised or a new one is published, the English, Spanish and French versions be produced together as a matter of course.
items.conf_reason: Literature reviews new and revised literature and new formats (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: Since 2022, Conference committee background is released at the same time in English, French and Spanish (p3692). The 2026 Final Report (p. 91) says the General Service Office is still working toward service material in all three languages.

items.title: Name discrimination as a safety issue in A.A.'s safety guidelines
items.summary: Proposes revising wording in the A.A. Guidelines on safety to state that discrimination members experience within A.A. is a safety issue that must be addressed, and that discrimination against marginalized communities violates Traditions One, Three and Five.
items.conf_reason: The Corrections committee reviewed the safety service piece in 2023 under the workload-sharing plan (2023 Final Report p. 41), and the safety guideline MG-25 grew out of a 2024 Corrections committee consideration (2026 Final Report p. 91).
items.note: Safety guidance for groups is service material, which is generally not Conference-approved; “A.A. Guidelines for Safety & A.A. Groups” (MG-25) grew out of a 2024 Corrections committee consideration (2026 Final Report p. 91).
items.differs: Withdrawn #7 proposed nearly the same statement for the safety pamphlet; this one targets the A.A. Guidelines on safety.
items.quote: Instances of discrimination experienced by members within A.A. are safety issues

items.title: Disclose what A.A. paid for the Everything A.A. app
items.summary: Asks for disclosure of how much money was spent buying the Everything A.A. app.
items.conf_reason: Finance reviews the budgets and financial reports of A.A. World Services and AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: The Service Manual lists the Everything AA app among digital platforms overseen by the A.A. World Services (AAWS) Services and Technology committee (p. 66). A 2025 proposal for an all-literature app or buying Everything AA (76th grid item 35) was not forwarded.
items.differs: #77 and #169 ask for standing disclosure rules for large purchases (#169 includes digital assets); this one asks only what the app cost.

items.title: Keep a workshop audio recording on the Everything A.A. app
items.summary: Asks that a workshop audio recording now on the Everything A.A. app, which the text names after its two presenters, be kept there in its current form.
items.conf_reason: App content is overseen by the A.A. World Services Services and Technology committee (Service Manual p. 66); likely handled at that board level.
items.note: The Everything AA app is one of the digital platforms overseen by the A.A. World Services (AAWS) Services and Technology committee (Service Manual p. 66).

items.title: Evaluate the All Programs Anonymous (APA) meeting-locator platform
items.summary: Wants the fitting A.A. World Services board or trustees' committee to look into APA (All Programs Anonymous), a tech platform meant to lead members to the actual meeting room, not only the building, and to recovery resources, then judge whether it is worth more study, development, testing or a referral.
items.conf_reason: Addressed to an A.A. World Services board or trustees' committee; that board oversees A.A.'s apps (Service Manual p. 66).
items.note: A.A.'s own meeting finder is the Meeting Guide app, overseen with aa.org by the A.A. World Services (AAWS) Services and Technology committee (Service Manual p. 66).
items.differs: #48 asks for All Programs Anonymous's age-based Twelve Steps material as Conference-approved literature; this one asks for an evaluation of its meeting-locator platform.

items.title: Review General Service Office staffing against current finances
items.summary: Asks for a review of General Service Office staffing levels, with adjustments so that staffing and personnel costs fit the current and projected finances of the service structure.
items.conf_reason: Finance reviews the A.A. World Services and Grapevine budgets (Service Manual p. 46); personnel is 65% of office operating expenses (2026 Final Report p. 26).
items.note: The General Service Office (GSO) has about 100 employees, 88 with A.A. World Services and 12 with Grapevine (Service Manual p. 87). In 2025, salaries, benefits and payroll taxes were 65% of GSO operating expenses (2026 Final Report p. 26).

items.title: Review the literature cross-references in Daily Reflections
items.summary: Asks for a thorough review of Daily Reflections so that its references to other A.A. literature are accurate and up to date.
items.conf_reason: Literature reviews revisions to existing recovery literature (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: The same wording was submitted for the 2026 Conference (76th grid item 28) and was not forwarded. Daily Reflections, built from members' writings, was approved in 1990 (p2691).

items.title: American Sign Language versions of the Service Manual and three pamphlets
items.summary: Asks that American Sign Language (ASL) versions be made of The A.A. Service Manual (BM-31) and three pamphlets: “The A.A. Group... Where It All Begins” (P-16), “The God Word” (P-86) and “A Brief Guide to A.A.” (P-42).
items.conf_reason: Treatment and Accessibilities covers accessibility needs (Service Manual p. 47); Report and Charter studied an ASL Service Manual in 2022-2023 (2023 Final Report p. 47).
items.note: By 2020 the Big Book and Twelve and Twelve had been released in American Sign Language (ASL) (2020 Final Report p. 11). In 2023 the Report and Charter committee reviewed a feasibility report on an ASL Service Manual (2023 Final Report p. 47).

items.title: Translate the Big Book into Ralik (Marshallese)
items.summary: Asks that the Big Book, Alcoholics Anonymous, be translated into Ralik, the western dialect of Marshallese.
items.conf_reason: Translations of Bill W.'s writings need no Conference approval (p2948); the trustees' International Committee, with no Conference counterpart, supports translations (Service Manual p. 59).
items.note: In 1962 the Conference adopted a translation report making how common alcoholism is among a language's speakers the criterion for choosing languages (p3251); in 2007 it noted that translations of Bill W.'s writings do not need Conference approval (p2948).

items.title: Move the General Service Office from New York to Akron
items.summary: Proposes moving the General Service Office from New York City to Akron, Ohio.
items.conf_reason: The 1994 decision against a committee to move the General Service Office (p1374) sits in the Finance section of the Advisory Actions booklet (M-39).
items.note: The General Service Office (GSO) is in New York City (Service Manual p. 87). A 1976 floor action authorized a relocation study; the 1977 and 1978 Conferences decided not to move GSO, and the 1994 Conference declined to form a relocation committee (p6076, p6077, p1374).

items.title: Explore an A.A.-run, privacy-focused artificial intelligence (AI) information tool
items.summary: Proposes exploring an artificial intelligence (AI) tool that A.A. controls and hosts itself on open-source software, with safeguards for anonymity, serving only as an information resource and not a substitute for sponsorship, meetings, professional care or human connection. Existing A.A. technology could be considered.
items.conf_reason: A guess: Public Information evaluates digital strategies for carrying the message (Service Manual p. 47); no Conference committee owns AI as such.
items.note: A.A. World Services' (AAWS) 2025 policy on artificial intelligence (AI) bars AI where sensitive personal information is involved and requires accuracy checks (2025 Final Report p. 13). In 2026 the trustees' General Service Conference committee did not enact open-source AI for committee selection, citing that policy (2026 Final Report p. 83).

items.title: Offer all communications in print and digital at one price, postage-free
items.summary: Asks the General Service Board, the General Service Office (GSO), A.A. World Services and AA Grapevine to issue every communication both electronically and in print, at the same price, with mailing or postage free.
items.conf_reason: A guess: pricing and free postage are financial; Finance reviews or initiates recommendations involving finances (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: New General Service Representatives get a digital GSR kit unless they ask for print; District Committee Members opt in to a mailed print kit (Service Manual pp. 118-119). Since 2017 the Final Report has an anonymity-protected digital edition beside the printed one (p3657).
items.differs: Broader than #128 (Advisory Actions booklet) and #175 (Service Manual in kits): it covers every communication from all four bodies.

items.title: Reprint an updated, indexed Advisory Actions booklet (M-39) every five years
items.summary: Asks for a new, current edition of the Advisory Actions compilation (M-39) in both print and electronic form, with an index, printed copies free to serving delegates, and a fresh edition every five years.
items.conf_reason: A guess: past decisions on the Advisory Actions summary (format, index, who receives it) came through Report and Charter (p4327, p4300).
items.note: The 1951-2022 compilation was reported available digitally on aa.org (2023 Final Report p. 60). In 2020 a trustees' committee took no action on a searchable database, noting Conference members had a searchable PDF (2020 Final Report p. 25). A 1971 action added an index (p4327).

items.title: Include the Service Manual free in general service representative and district kits
items.summary: Asks that The A.A. Service Manual/Twelve Concepts for World Service (BM-31) be included at no cost in the kits sent to General Service Representatives (GSRs) and District Committee Members (DCMs), arriving automatically unless the person opts out.
items.conf_reason: A guess: Report and Charter is responsible for The A.A. Service Manual (Service Manual p. 47) and in 2025 discussed whether the printed kits for general service representatives should include it (2025 Final Report p. 51); the cost side could also reach Finance.
items.note: The General Service Office (GSO) sends complimentary kits to newly listed general service representatives (GSRs) and district committee members (DCMs) (Service Manual p. 71). The GSR kit includes the manual (p. 12) but is digital unless print is requested; DCMs opt in to print (pp. 118-119). The same request without the opt-out (76th grid item 69) was not forwarded.

items.title: Use the new contributions platform to inform members and gather input
items.summary: Proposes expanding the new online contributions platform so that A.A. can tell the members who use it about significant actions directly and collect their advisory, non-binding opinions.
items.conf_reason: A guess: direct, non-binding member input would affect how the Conference hears the Fellowship, a matter of Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: In 2025-26 the A.A. World Services (AAWS) board's Services and Technology Committee evaluated alternative online contribution platforms and discussed opt-in communication outreach, mindful of privacy (2026 Final Report p. 17). The proposal does not name the platform.
items.differs: #147 asks the General Service Board to study a voluntary, anonymous e-mail-type system for the same purpose; this one would extend the contributions platform.

items.title: Release A.A. Comes of Age as a digital audiobook
items.summary: Asks A.A. World Services to consider publishing A.A. Comes of Age, Bill W.'s book on A.A.'s history, as an official digital audiobook on current platforms such as Audible, Apple Books, Kobo and Google Play.
items.conf_reason: Literature reviews new formats of existing literature, including digital and audiovisual (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: A 1985 action sought a cassette (p2592). A.A. World Services (AAWS) lists an e-book and a CD album (2024 Final Report p. 61; 2026 Final Report p. 118). In 2025 the Treatment and Accessibilities committee suggested an aa.org audiobook of the CD version (2025 Final Report p. 52).

items.title: Apply the Double-Trouble directory rule to the Meeting Guide app
items.summary: Asks A.A. World Services to consider stating that the 1986 and 1987 Conference guidance keeping Double-Trouble groups out of A.A. directories also applies to its Meeting Guide app.

responds_to.what: Double-Trouble groups not to be listed in A.A. directories
Reaffirmed the 1986 action and removed existing Double-Trouble listings

items.conf_reason: A guess: Public Information reviews the yearly Meeting Guide app report (2026 Final Report p. 51); the 1986-87 directory actions came from Report and Charter.
items.note: The 1986 action kept Double-Trouble groups out of A.A. directories; the 1987 action, defining them as groups with outside affiliation, reaffirmed it and removed listings (p4462, p4481). Printed directories ended in 2021 (p4785). Meeting Guide relays listings from local service entities (Service Manual p. 168).

items.title: End print Grapevine and La Viña; keep digital and printable editions
items.summary: Proposes that AA Grapevine stop printing paper copies of Grapevine and La Viña, keep the digital and online editions of both magazines, and add a version members can download and print at home.
items.conf_reason: Grapevine and La Viña reviews the magazines' development, circulation, material and format (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: AA Grapevine aims to pay its way through subscriptions and sales; La Viña shortfalls are covered by the General Service Board (Service Manual p. 68). A survey on the viability of Grapevine products will report progress to the 77th Conference (2026 Final Report p. 46).

items.title: Raise Grapevine prices so it fully pays its own way
items.summary: Proposes raising the price of the Grapevine so that it becomes self-supporting, counting all of its costs: the printed magazine, digital and online subscriptions, the podcast, and anything else needed to run the Grapevine.
items.conf_reason: A guess: past Grapevine price decisions came through the Grapevine committee (p1578); Finance also reviews the Grapevine budget (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: AA Grapevine takes no contributions and relies on subscriptions and sales (Service Manual p. 68). In 2026 the Grapevine committee suggested the Grapevine and General Service Boards explore ways to support Grapevine services that earn no revenue (2026 Final Report pp. 46-47).

items.title: Restore “men and women” in place of “people” in the Preamble
items.summary: Asks that the A.A. Preamble drop the word “people” and again describe A.A. as a fellowship of “men and women,” the wording used before 2021.

responds_to.what: Floor actions replacing “men and women” with “people” and sending it to the General Service Board

items.conf_reason: The Preamble is copyrighted by AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 24) and the 2021 Preamble actions are filed under Grapevine and La Viña.
items.note: The 2021 Conference replaced “men and women” with “people” by floor action and sent it to the General Service Board (p1710, p1711). The same wording was submitted for 2026 (76th grid item 76) and not forwarded to the Conference.
items.differs: Same request as #59 and #206 in other words; #205 asks to keep “people”; #20 asks the Fellowship to choose among options.

items.title: Ask the Fellowship which Preamble wording it wants
items.summary: Asks the Conference to have the appropriate committee(s) gather the conscience of groups, districts and areas on three options: keep the current Preamble, return to the wording used before the 2021 actions, or drop any definition of the Fellowship; then report results and suggestions to the 2027 Conference.

responds_to.what: Floor actions that rewrote the Preamble's opening and adopted “people”

items.conf_reason: The Preamble is copyrighted by AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 24); the 2021 Preamble actions and 2021-22 Preamble discussions were in Grapevine and La Viña.
items.note: 2021 floor actions approved an opening “In Alcoholics Anonymous we share” and “people”; a third sent “people” to the board (2021 Final Report p. 59). A 2024 floor action for area discussion was recommitted to a trustees' committee or board (2024 Final Report pp. 52-53).
items.differs: Unlike #18, #59 and #206 (restore “men and women”) and #205 (keep “people”), it asks for a Fellowship-wide consultation on three options.

items.title: Add “particular faith” to the Preamble's neutrality sentence
items.summary: Proposes adding the words “particular faith” to the Preamble sentence listing what A.A. is not allied with, citing the Foreword to the First Edition of the Big Book as the source of that wording.
targets: Big Book Foreword to the First Edition
items.conf_reason: The Preamble is copyrighted by AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 24); Preamble actions are filed under Grapevine and La Viña.
items.note: A Grapevine editor wrote the Preamble in 1947, basing it on the Big Book's first-edition Foreword (Service Manual p. 170). It says A.A. is not allied with any sect, denomination, politics, organization or institution (p. II). The 1987 Conference chose no changes or additions (p1626).
items.differs: Unlike #18, #59, #205 and #206, which concern “people” in the first sentence, this targets the neutrality sentence.
items.quote: reinserting the words “particular faith” into the neutrality statement

items.title: Restore “men and women” in place of “people” in the Preamble
items.summary: Asks to take the word “people” out of the A.A. Preamble and put back “men and women,” the wording in use before the 2021 Conference.

responds_to.what: Floor actions replacing “men and women” with “people” and sending it to the General Service Board

items.conf_reason: The Preamble is copyrighted by AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 24) and the 2021 Preamble actions are filed under Grapevine and La Viña.
items.note: The word “people” came from a 2021 floor action, which a further floor action sent to the General Service Board for approval (p1710, p1711). A request in the same terms was not forwarded to the 2026 Conference (76th grid item 76).
items.differs: Same request as #18 and #206, worded differently; #205 asks to keep “people”; #20 asks for a Fellowship consultation.

items.title: Keep “people” in the Preamble rather than “men and women”
items.summary: Proposes, on behalf of a group, that the Preamble keep the word “people,” which replaced “men and women” in 2021.

responds_to.what: Floor action adopting “people” in the Preamble (reaffirm)

items.conf_reason: The Preamble is copyrighted by AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 24) and the 2021 Preamble actions are filed under Grapevine and La Viña.
items.note: “People” was adopted by 2021 floor actions (p1710, p1711). In 2025 the Conference declined to consider a floor action asking the board to adopt a different Preamble, opening “In Alcoholics Anonymous, we share” (2025 Final Report p. 54).
items.differs: The opposite of #18, #59 and #206, which ask to restore “men and women”; #20 asks the Fellowship to weigh the options.

items.title: Restore “men and women” in place of “people” in the Preamble
items.summary: Asks that the Preamble's word “people” be changed back to “men and women,” returning to the wording used before 2021.

responds_to.what: Floor actions replacing “men and women” with “people” and sending it to the General Service Board

items.conf_reason: The Preamble is copyrighted by AA Grapevine (Service Manual p. 24) and the 2021 Preamble actions are filed under Grapevine and La Viña.
items.note: In 2022 the Grapevine and La Viña committee said it was too early to measure the Preamble change's impact, as many members were still uninformed or ambivalent (2022 Final Report p. 84). The change itself came from 2021 floor actions (p1710, p1711).
items.differs: Same request as #18 and #59 in different words; #205 asks to keep “people”; #20 asks the Fellowship to weigh the options.

items.title: Tag Grapevine Story Archive articles about Bill W. and Dr. Bob
items.summary: Wants Grapevine to label Story Archive pieces by or about the co-founders with the Tradition and Step topics they touch (Tradition Four; Steps One, Four, Six, Seven, Nine), so searching by those topics finds them.
items.conf_reason: Grapevine and La Viña seeks suggestions on any area of the magazines and related material (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: The Story Archive holds almost every Grapevine article since June 1944, including every one by Bill W., browsable by department, topic or date (Service Manual p. 84). Grapevine reported finishing story tagging in 2017 (2018 Final Report p. 87).

items.title: Five-year subscription audit of Grapevine and La Viña
items.summary: Asks the Grapevine and La Viña Committee to audit five years of subscriptions to both magazines: yearly new, renewed, lapsed and cancelled subscriptions, delivery problems, replacements, service complaints, and subscription income and costs, with Grapevine and La Viña reported separately for comparison.
items.conf_reason: This committee reviews the development and circulation of Grapevine and La Viña and meets jointly with the Grapevine board (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: A 2025 action asked the Conference Grapevine and La Viña committee to review both magazines' five-year plans yearly, with at least five years of financial history (p1713). The Grapevine board's 2026 report lists each magazine's subscription totals by print, complete, online and app (2026 Final Report p. 23).

items.title: Plan for a comparable number of La Viña book titles by 2029
items.summary: Citing the principle of spiritual parity, asks AA Grapevine, Inc. to make and carry out a plan so that by 2029 La Viña offers about as many book titles as Grapevine does, reusing La Viña material the Conference has already approved where that fits.

responds_to.what: La Viña to move toward spiritual parity with the Grapevine

items.conf_reason: This committee considers topics for future Grapevine/La Viña books and reaches Spanish-speaking alcoholics through La Viña (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: A 2010 action set the goal that La Viña “achieve spiritual parity” with the Grapevine, starting with a 68-page bimonthly trial in 2011 (p1677). In 2026 the Conference committee forwarded to the Grapevine board a suggested La Viña book of stories, Despertares Espirituales (working title) (2026 Final Report p. 46).
items.quote: principle of spiritual parity

items.title: Replace the “Hope: Alcoholics Anonymous” video with a shorter update
items.summary: Asks for a newer, shorter version of the video “Hope: Alcoholics Anonymous” to replace the current one.

responds_to.what: approval of the revised Hope video

items.conf_reason: The grid sends it to trustees' Public Information, whose Conference counterpart is Public Information (Service Manual p. 47); earlier Hope actions were Treatment actions (p2089).
items.note: The Conference accepted the video in 1990 for members carrying the message into treatment facilities (p2036) and approved a revision in 2009 (p2089). In 2024 the Conference Finance committee, under a workload-sharing plan, found it still relevant and useful and chose not to update it (2024 Final Report p. 43).

items.title: More guidance on the Traditions for A.A. social media pages
items.summary: Asks for fuller guidance on following the Traditions on social media pages that use the A.A. name and are run by groups, districts and areas.
items.conf_reason: Public Information evaluates digital strategies and social media efforts (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: In 2026 the Conference approved a revised “Understanding Anonymity” (P-47), retitled “Anonymity – Our Spiritual Foundation,” after a 2025 request that it cover social media (p4268, p4277). A 2022 revision had already suggested that A.A. social media pages be private (p4198).

items.title: Resume publishing A.A. group and membership estimates in the Final Report
items.summary: Asks the Conference to recommend that the General Service Office (GSO) go back to printing, in each year's Final Report, an estimate of total A.A. groups and members, using low-cost estimation methods. The proposal says this was done every year from 1951 through 2021.
items.conf_reason: Public Information reviews membership survey data (Service Manual p. 47). Report and Charter, which reviews the Final Report, could also take it.
items.note: The 2017–2022 Final Reports each print a table of estimated A.A. groups and members, the last one as of December 31, 2021 (2022 Final Report p. 108). Later reports do not. In 2026 an A.A. World Services (AAWS) working group discussed improving the service materials on membership estimates (2026 Final Report p. 17).

items.title: Add “and the internet” to the short form of Tradition Eleven
items.summary: Proposes adding the internet to the list of media at the end of the short form of Tradition Eleven, which now names press, radio and films.

responds_to.what: kept the wording of Tradition Eleven unchanged
affirmed that Tradition Eleven's closing words cover the internet and social media

items.conf_reason: Past actions on Tradition Eleven's wording and the internet were Public Information actions (p3819, p4137).
items.note: Changing a Tradition needs the written consent of three-quarters of A.A. groups (Service Manual p. 124). In 2013 the Conference affirmed that the closing words cover the internet and social media (p4137). A 2026-cycle request to add “and social media” was not forwarded (2026 Final Report p. 115).
items.quote: and the internet

items.title: Make an Area 36 movie-theater public service announcement available Fellowship-wide
items.summary: Proposes that a 30-second public service announcement (PSA) shown in movie theaters by the Area 36 (Southern Minnesota) Public Information committee become an approved PSA video for all of the U.S./Canada Fellowship, posted on aa.org.
items.conf_reason: Public Information reviews public information pamphlets and public service announcements (PSAs) (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: In 2025 the Conference asked that three A.A. Australia videos be adapted for U.S./Canada platforms (p4267). In the 2026 cycle trustees' Public Information took no action on a request for cable-TV PSAs of 30 seconds or less, noting 15- and 30-second PSAs exist (2026 Final Report p. 115).
items.differs: #140 asks for a new, uniform public information piece with QR codes and a campaign. This one asks to adopt an existing video public service announcement (PSA) made by an area.

items.title: A shared public information piece with QR codes, plus a campaign
items.summary: Asks that A.A. produce a public information service piece with a simple, consistent message and QR codes, usable across the whole U.S./Canada service structure, and that A.A. use it in a public information campaign.
items.conf_reason: Public Information works through public media and reviews public information pamphlets and public service announcements (PSAs) (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: The General Service Office (GSO) recently created business-card-sized Young People Service Cards with QR codes for the Meeting Guide app and offers the template for local use (2026 Final Report p. 68). QR codes were added to all new Conference-approved pamphlets (2026 Final Report p. 15).
items.differs: #121 asks to adopt an existing area-made public service announcement (PSA) video. This one asks for a new, uniform service piece with QR codes and a campaign that uses it.

items.title: One-year wait before new director or general service trustee roles
items.summary: Asks the Conference to consider requiring that candidates for new nontrustee director and general service trustee positions have been rotated out of earlier Conference-level or board-level service for at least one year.
items.conf_reason: The Trustees committee reviews résumés of nominees for the General Service Board and the corporate directors (Service Manual p. 48).
items.note: Delegates wait one year after their last Conference before standing for trustee (Service Manual p. 63; p5047). General service trustees are chosen from current or past nontrustee directors (Service Manual p. 56). In the 2026 cycle trustees' Nominating took no action on similar waiting-period requests (2026 Final Report p. 110).

items.title: Censure the 2026 General Service Conference and its actions
items.summary: Proposes a formal censure of the 2026 General Service Conference and of all actions brought forward by “the panel.”

responds_to.what: the 2026 Conference and all of its actions

items.conf_reason: The grid sends it to trustees' Nominating, which sent its 2026 censure-motion reports to the Conference Committee on Trustees (2026 Final Report p. 109).
items.note: Concept III says the Conference can censure or even reorganize the trustees (Service Manual p. C-10). Censure proposals in 1995, 2023 and 2025 concerned the General Service Board (p5275; 2023 Final Report p. 49; 2025 Final Report p. 5). A 2026 action asked for a documented censure-motion process, reporting in 2027 (p5635).

items.title: Print the 2022 board reorganization procedure in the Service Manual
items.summary: Asks that the 2022 Conference-approved procedure for partly or fully reorganizing the General Service Board, A.A. World Services (AAWS) or AA Grapevine boards be added as an appendix to The A.A. Service Manual, with a footnote in Concept III pointing to it.

responds_to.what: approval of the suggested procedure to reorganize the General Service Board and the corporate boards

items.conf_reason: Report and Charter reviews The A.A. Service Manual (Service Manual p. 47). It is routed to trustees' Nominating; the 2022 procedure was a Trustees action.
items.note: The 2022 Conference approved this procedure as one acceptable path, with the final process set by whichever Conference considers a reorganization (p5581). Under Charter Article 4, three-quarters of Conference members voting can reorganize the board (Service Manual p. 124). The 2026–2028 Manual does not print the procedure.

items.title: Disclose General Service Office purchases over $500,000; discourage nondisclosure agreements
items.summary: Asks that the General Service Office (GSO) be required to tell the Fellowship about any asset purchase over $500,000 and explain it. It also asks that GSO be strongly discouraged from signing nondisclosure agreements that could limit transparency with the Fellowship.
items.conf_reason: Finance reviews or initiates Conference recommendations that involve finances (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: A 2025 action asked that the board's Quarterly Financial Report add details on capital projects and maintenance costs (p1497). In the 2026 cycle trustees' Finance did not forward a request for fuller financial reporting, citing confidentiality and the existing annual and quarterly reports (2026 Final Report p. 78).
items.differs: #169 asks the board for a broader published policy on significant acquisitions and commitments, including digital assets. This one sets a $500,000 disclosure threshold and addresses nondisclosure agreements.

items.title: Self-support literature for online and clubhouse meetings
items.summary: Asks that self-support literature be expanded to explain how online meetings and meetings held in clubhouses can contribute both to the General Service Office (GSO) and to A.A.'s conscience.

responds_to.what: GSO does not accept contributions from clubs, but groups meeting in clubs may contribute in the group's name

items.conf_reason: Changes to the self-support pamphlet have been Finance actions (p1470, p1474), and Finance handles recommendations involving finances (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: A 1972 floor action says the General Service Office (GSO) does not accept contributions from clubs, though groups meeting in clubs may give in the group's name (p1235). The self-support pamphlet added Q&As on online contributions in 2017 and on a “virtual” basket in 2020 (p1470, p1474).
items.differs: #96 and #153 ask that the pamphlet The A.A. Group (P-16) cover online groups. This one asks for self-support literature on how online and clubhouse meetings contribute.

items.title: Reserve Fund: rebuilding plan after 12 months below 9–12 months
items.summary: Proposes that if the Reserve Fund stays below the 9-to-12-month range set in the board's October 2022 reserve fund policy for 12 months in a row, the trustees' Finance and Budgetary Committee must bring the Conference a plan and timeline to rebuild it. This would replace current language.
items.conf_reason: Finance handles Conference recommendations involving finances (Service Manual p. 46). Past Reserve Fund limits were Finance actions (p1333, p1417).
items.note: The Conference caps the fund at one year's expenses (Service Manual p. 65). A 2022 board policy set a goal of 9–12 months (2023 Final Report p. 21). Trustees' Finance did not forward a similar 2026-cycle item, saying it could restrict the board's legal duties (2026 Final Report pp. 78–79).
items.differs: #134 sets a 3-month floor with a two-quarter trigger; #181 sets a 9-month minimum. This one uses a 12-month trigger and the 9–12 month range.

items.title: Reserve Fund: three-month minimum, with a recovery plan
items.summary: Proposes a three-month minimum for the Reserve Fund. After two straight quarters below it, the General Service Board would, at its next quarterly meeting, report to the Conference Committee on Finance a plan and timeline for getting back to three months, then report yearly until the fund reaches 4.5 months.

responds_to.what: decided that the Reserve Fund have no lower limit, since the auditor comments on its adequacy

items.conf_reason: Finance handles Conference recommendations involving finances (Service Manual p. 46). Past Reserve Fund limits were Finance actions (p1333).
items.note: A 1987 action limited the fund to at most one year's expenses, with no lower limit, since auditors judge its adequacy (p1333). In January 2026 the fund stood at 5.92 months, projected near five months by April 2026 if the full drawdown was used (2026 Final Report p. 14).
items.differs: #133 and #181 use the 9–12 month range or a 9-month minimum. This one sets a lower 3-month floor, a two-quarter trigger and a 4.5-month target for yearly reports.

items.title: Board policy on disclosing major acquisitions, including digital assets
items.summary: Asks the Conference to request that the General Service Board adopt and publish a consistent policy on timely financial reporting for significant acquisitions and commitments, including digital assets: costs, funding, financial effects, approval authority, key terms, data and privacy effects, and periodic updates, while protecting information that must stay confidential.
items.conf_reason: Finance reviews or initiates Conference recommendations that involve finances (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: A 2025 action asked for capital-project and maintenance-cost details in the board's Quarterly Financial Report (p1497). The board authorizes Reserve Fund withdrawals on its Finance committee's recommendation (Service Manual p. 65). A 2026-cycle request for more financial detail was not forwarded (2026 Final Report p. 78).
items.differs: #77 sets a $500,000 disclosure threshold and addresses nondisclosure agreements. This one asks the board for a general published policy on significant acquisitions and commitments, including digital assets.

items.title: Reserve Fund: use its income only while the fund holds six months
items.summary: Asks the Conference to revise the 1967 action that lets the General Service Board use Reserve Fund investment income for any purpose it authorizes, adding a condition: such use is allowed only while the fund balance equals at least six months of expenses.

responds_to.what: revise: the board may use Reserve Fund investment income for purposes it authorizes

items.conf_reason: Finance reviews or initiates Conference recommendations that involve finances (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: Under the 1967 action (p1210) the board decides how Reserve Fund investment income is used. At end-2025 the fund held 6.17 months of expenses (2026 Final Report p. 26). Trustees took no action on a 76th-cycle proposal limiting that use (same report p. 78).
items.differs: #133 and #134 require replenishment plans (below 9–12 and 3 months) and #181 sets a 9-month minimum; this one instead limits use of investment income below six months.
items.quote: as long as the Reserve Fund Balance is at least 6 months

items.title: Reserve Fund: nine-month minimum
items.summary: Proposes that the Reserve Fund have a minimum of nine months of operating expenses, which the submitter says matches the floor the board has used for years, alongside the 12-month maximum the Conference has already set.

responds_to.what: adds a lower limit to the rule that the fund not exceed one year's expenses

items.conf_reason: Finance reviews or initiates Conference recommendations that involve finances (Service Manual p. 46); the Reserve Fund ceiling was set by Finance actions (p1333).
items.note: The Service Manual limits the fund to no more than one year's combined operating expenses and states no minimum (p. 65; 1987 action p1333). The 2026 Final Report (p. 14) cites a nine-to-12-month target range, with the fund near six months.
items.differs: #133 and #134 add replenishment plans (below 9–12 and 3 months) and #179 ties income use to six months; this one sets a 9-month floor with no plan.

items.title: Reprint Bill W.'s “Three Talks to Medical Societies” pamphlet
items.summary: Asks that the retired pamphlet “Three Talks to Medical Societies” by co-founder Bill W. be printed again and widely shared, with a cover reference to the Lasker Award from the American Public Health Association, stressing that alcoholism is an illness. Submitted in Spanish with an English translation.

responds_to.what: reverse the retirement of the pamphlet

items.conf_reason: The Cooperation with the Professional Community committee recommended retiring this pamphlet in 2017 (p1069; Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: The 2017 Conference retired it (p1069; 2017 Final Report p. 9) after trustees called its language dated (p. 44). Trustees took no action on a 2024 revival request; watermarked copies are available from Archives for personal use (2024 Final Report p. 74).

items.title: Merge two corrections publications into one pamphlet with speaker guidance
items.summary: Proposes combining two publications on carrying the message into correctional facilities (F-5 and F-108) into one pamphlet that adds speaking guidance like that in “A.A. in Treatment Settings” (P-27), especially member qualifications and do's and don'ts, plus background on types and functions of correctional facilities.
items.conf_reason: Corrections recommends updates to corrections materials and reviews service to groups in correctional facilities (Service Manual p. 46).
items.note: P-27 is the pamphlet “A.A. in Treatment Settings” (2026 Final Report p. 73). In 1994 the Conference added guidelines for presentations to corrections professionals and inmates to the Correctional Facilities Workbook (p1860).

items.title: Hold an online Special Forum for members of online groups
items.summary: Asks the Conference, on behalf of Area 51, to consider creating an online Special Forum designed mainly for members of online A.A. groups that are not part of any of the eight regions of the U.S./Canada service structure.
items.conf_reason: The International Conventions/Regional Forums committee offers input on Regional, Local and Special Forums (Service Manual p. 48).
items.note: Special Forums serve members who would not normally attend a Regional or Local Forum, or meet needs of culture, language or geography (Service Manual p. 62). A one-day online Special Forum for Deaf members was held January 17, 2026 (2026 Final Report p. 98).
items.differs: #22 and #112 ask for a virtual delegate area for online groups; this one asks only for a sharing event, not a place in the service structure.

items.title: Charge a registration fee for Regional Forums
items.summary: Asks the Conference to consider charging attendees a registration fee for Regional Forums.

responds_to.what: would change the free registration described in the Service Manual's Regional Forums section

items.conf_reason: The International Conventions/Regional Forums committee offers input on how Regional Forums are run (Service Manual p. 48).
items.note: The Service Manual says there is no registration fee for Regional Forums and the General Service Board pays for meeting rooms (p. 62); a 2015 action added the section describing free registration (p4742).

items.title: Add the Lord's Prayer back to Big Meeting closing options
items.summary: Asks that the Lord's Prayer be offered again, alongside the current closing options for the Big Meetings at the International Convention, giving the meeting chair more choice.

responds_to.what: add the Lord's Prayer to the six Big Meeting closing options

items.conf_reason: The International Conventions/Regional Forums committee plans Conventions and recommended the 2024 closing options (Service Manual p. 48; p2282).
items.note: Before 2024 chairs could close Big Meetings with the Lord's Prayer, Serenity Prayer or Responsibility Statement (2024 Final Report p. 86); the 2024 action's six options omit it (p2282). Trustees took no action on two 2025 restore requests (2026 Final Report p. 97).
items.differs: #154 (withdrawn) argued the Lord's Prayer conflicts with the Preamble; this one asks to add it back as one choice among the current options.

items.title: Enforce sobriety time for district, intergroup and general service representative roles
items.summary: Proposed enforcing A.A. guidance on how long a member should be sober before holding district or intergroup offices, and suggested applying it to general service representative (GSR) positions too. Removed with the submitter's approval.
items.conf_reason: Suggested sobriety for general service representatives (GSRs) and district committee members appears in the Service Manual, which Report and Charter reviews (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: The Service Manual suggests general service representatives have at least two years of continuous sobriety (p. 7) and district committee members four or five years (p. 15). Intergroup/central offices provide local services separate from general service committees (p. 25).

items.title: Name discrimination as a safety issue in the safety pamphlet
items.summary: Proposed revising the current safety pamphlet to adopt a diversity and inclusion statement: that discrimination within A.A. is a safety issue to be addressed, and that discrimination against marginalized communities violates Traditions One, Three and Five. Superseded by proposed agenda item 217.
items.conf_reason: The Corrections committee reviewed the safety service piece in 2023 under the workload-sharing plan (2023 Final Report p. 41), and the safety guideline MG-25 grew out of a 2024 Corrections committee consideration (2026 Final Report p. 91).
items.note: “Safety and A.A.: Our Common Welfare” is A.A. World Services (A.A.W.S.) service material, generally not Conference-approved. The 2023 Corrections committee reviewed it and suggested revisions (2023 Final Report p. 41); the 2026 Final Report traces the guideline MG-25, “A.A. Guidelines for Safety & A.A. Groups,” to a 2024 Corrections committee consideration (2026 Final Report p. 91).
items.differs: #217, which replaced it, names “A.A. Guidelines on Safety and A.A.” and drops the opening reference to the spirit of Tradition Three.
items.quote: instances of discrimination within A.A. are safety issues

items.title: Upgrade an area's Zoom, translation and hybrid equipment
items.summary: Moved that, following an earlier motion on translation access, the submitter's area research and plan upgrades to its Zoom and translation equipment, offer consistent hybrid access to area events, and keep equipment area-owned per the Seventh Tradition. Removed with the submitter's approval.
items.conf_reason: Concerns one area's own equipment and events rather than a Conference-wide matter.

items.title: Audit A.A. pamphlets for repetition and Tradition concerns
items.summary: Proposes an audit of A.A.'s pamphlets to find material that repeats itself and to identify content the submitter believes conflicts with the Twelve Traditions.
items.conf_reason: Literature reviews and recommends revisions to existing literature (Service Manual p. 47).
items.note: In 1992 the Conference kept a subcommittee reviewing all approved material to discourage unnecessary duplication (p2718; M-39 p. 93). In 2016-2017 it set up a yearly review of recovery literature by the trustees' Literature Committee (p3020, p3027).

items.title: Print the 2022 board reorganization procedure in the Service Manual
items.summary: Asks that the 2022 Conference-approved procedure for partly or fully reorganizing the General Service Board, A.A. World Services (AAWS) or AA Grapevine boards be added as an appendix to The A.A. Service Manual, with a footnote in Concept III pointing to it.

responds_to.what: approval of the suggested procedure to reorganize the General Service Board and the corporate boards

items.conf_reason: Report and Charter reviews The A.A. Service Manual (Service Manual p. 47). It is routed to trustees' Nominating; the 2022 procedure was a Trustees action.
items.note: The 2022 Conference approved this procedure as one acceptable path, with the final process set by whichever Conference considers a reorganization (p5581). Under Charter Article 4, three-quarters of Conference members voting can reorganize the board (Service Manual p. 124). The 2026–2028 Manual does not print the procedure.

items.outcome: Item removed as a Human Resources matter not suitable for wider distribution

items.title: Committee motions passed at the Conference wait until the next year
items.summary: Proposes that motions coming out of Conference committees and passed during the Conference week be placed on the following year's agenda and not take effect in the current year.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: A committee recommendation is presented in the committee report, automatically seconded and needs a two-thirds vote (Service Manual p. 175); approved Advisory Actions go to the General Service Board, which affirms them and sends them on for implementation (p. 43).

items.title: Floor motions passed at the Conference go to a committee, then wait a year
items.summary: Proposes that a floor motion passed during the Conference be sent to the matching committee; if the committee approves it, it would go on the next year's agenda rather than take effect that year.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 rule on late floor matters came from it (p3457).
items.note: Today a floor action's maker gets two minutes, the Conference may decline to consider it, and it needs a two-thirds vote (Service Manual pp. 174-175). In 2025 there were 12 floor actions: one passed, nine declined, two recommitted (2025 Final Report p. 5).

items.title: New floor and committee matters go to next year's agenda
items.summary: Asks the Conference to consider a process under which substantive committee recommendations and floor actions raising new policy, structural, financial, governance or literature matters, not already considered through the regular committee process, become proposed agenda items for the following year's Conference instead of being decided that week.
items.conf_reason: Policy/Admissions examines Conference policy (Service Manual p. 47); the 1986 practice for late floor matters came from Policy/Admissions (p3457).
items.note: A 1986 action sends weighty, long-term or costly matters raised in the final hours to the next year's committee (p3457). A 2026 recommendation that committees may defer items to a later Conference was committed to the General Service Board (2026 Final Report p. 42).

items.outcome: Item removed – no relevant Conference or Committee action introduced

items.title: Statement that the Lord's Prayer conflicts with the Preamble
items.summary: States that the Lord's Prayer conflicts with the Preamble's statement that A.A. is not allied with any sect or denomination, and that as a Christian prayer it excludes non-Christians and nonbelievers and creates barriers for newcomers. Withdrawn; it contained no requested action.
items.conf_reason: If it concerns International Convention Big Meetings, closing options there come through the International Conventions/Regional Forums committee (p2282; Service Manual p. 48).
items.note: The 2024 Conference set six ways to close International Convention Big Meetings, none of them the Lord's Prayer (p2282). Proposed agenda item 198 in this grid asks to add it back.
items.differs: #198 asks to add the Lord's Prayer back to the Big Meeting options; this one argues the opposite view and asked for no action.

items.title: Reconsider the Plain Language Big Book's Conference-approved status
items.summary: Asks the Conference to reconsider whether the Plain Language Big Book should keep its status as Conference-approved literature. Submitted for the 2026 Conference and held for 2027 under a 2025 Advisory Action.

responds_to.what: reconsider the approval of the Plain Language Big Book

items.conf_reason: The 2025 actions route Plain Language Big Book proposals through the trustees' Literature Committee to the Conference Literature committee (p3128, p3129).
items.note: The 2024 Conference approved the Plain Language Big Book (p3121). The 2025 Conference held proposals to withdraw or change it for the 77th Conference (p3128; 2025 Final Report p. 38), so trustees took no action in 2026 (2026 Final Report p. 104).
items.differs: #2025-86 asks to discontinue the book outright and #2025-108 to replace it with an annotated Big Book; this one asks only for reconsideration.

items.title: Discontinue the Plain Language Big Book as approved literature
items.summary: Asks that the Plain Language Big Book, which the submitter calls an interpretation and rewording of the Big Book, be dropped as Conference-approved literature, with no further circulation, printing or revision in A.A. Submitted for 2026 and held for 2027 under a 2025 Advisory Action.

responds_to.what: rescind the approval of the Plain Language Big Book

items.conf_reason: The 2025 actions route Plain Language Big Book proposals through the trustees' Literature Committee to the Conference Literature committee (p3128, p3129).
items.note: Trustees took no action in 2026, citing the 2025 action holding such proposals for the 77th Conference (2026 Final Report p. 106). In 2025 they took no action on similar rescission requests so members could first read the book (2025 Final Report pp. 106-107).
items.differs: #2025-7 asks only to reconsider the status and #2025-108 to replace the book; #60 in this grid would suspend the first edition until a second.

items.title: Replace the Plain Language Big Book with an annotated Big Book
items.summary: Proposes retiring the Plain Language Big Book and publishing a Big Book with columns of simple explanation beside the original text, titled “The Big Book Explained: A Useful Guide” and edited by a qualified sober alcoholic who knows the original well. Held from 2026 for 2027.

responds_to.what: retire the Plain Language Big Book approved in 2024 and replace it

items.conf_reason: The 2025 actions route Plain Language Big Book proposals through the trustees' Literature Committee to the Conference Literature committee (p3128, p3129).
items.note: Trustees took no action in 2026 because of the 2025 deferral (p3128; 2026 Final Report p. 107). The 2026 Conference Literature committee asked that page references to the original Big Book be considered for the Plain Language Big Book (2026 Final Report p. 49).
items.differs: #44 and #113 pair the Plain Language Big Book with the original and #184 has a credentialed member revise it; #106 asks for an annotated Big Book without mentioning the Plain Language Big Book. This one retires it for a new annotated Big Book.
items.quote: The Big Book Explained: A Useful Guide

observations: The Big Book and core texts lead: 121 of the 222 rows with text (219 numbered items plus 3 deferred from 2025) are about them, 101 on protecting or changing the text, such as Charter protection (32) and the 2026 “Eskimo” change (10). Last cycle such items were 10 of 110.

How changes get decided comes next: 40 rows ask for Fellowship review before Big Book changes (25, e.g. #86, #87, #93) or for floor actions and late committee recommendations to wait a year (15, e.g. #149, #172). The 76th cycle had neither.

Same wording, many senders: 32 of the 221 numbered items repeat another item (25 word for word, 7 but for a typo, a few words or a cut-off ending), leaving 189 distinct wordings. 27 are under consideration; 5 were withdrawn as superseded (#15, #41, #80, #81, #83).
Most came in the last two weeks: Of the 219 numbered items with a received date, 120 (55%) arrived Sept 17–30 and 32 on Sept 30 itself; only 13 had arrived by June 30.

Last year’s ideas come back: Eight items repeat or rework proposals not forwarded in the 76th cycle (#18, #50, #59, #104, #133, #166, #175, #198); #200 revisits a 2024 proposal, and #219 and #220 ask that earlier ones be brought back.

Who sent them: 160 of the 190 distinct texts (counting the 3 deferred from 2025) do not say. The only item from the Southwest Region, Area 65’s region, is #201, from two districts in Area 25 (Kansas).

forwarded_items.title: Remove a Dr. Bob quotation from the general service representative (GSR) chapter of The A.A. Service Manual
forwarded_items.outcome: No action. The trustees' General Service Conference Committee sent it to the Conference Committee on Report and Charter, which took no action: it found the quotation well placed in its section and said it conveys appreciation for the love of service.

forwarded_items.title: Study a less costly location for the General Service Conference
forwarded_items.outcome: No Advisory Action; a progress report was requested. The trustees' General Service Conference Committee sent it to the Conference Committee on Policy and Admissions, but under the 2025-2026 Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) plan the Conference Committee on Finance heard it. That committee asked the general manager, the trustees' General Service Conference Committee and the Meeting, Events and Travel Services (METS) team to keep exploring ways to cut Conference costs, including a hybrid format (online plus in person in New York City), and to bring a progress report with options and the estimated savings of each to the 2027 Conference Committee on Finance.

forwarded_items.title: Serving as an area trusted servant while living outside the area
forwarded_items.outcome: No action. The trustees' General Service Conference Committee sent it to Policy and Admissions; under the Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) plan the Conference Committee on Archives heard it. The committee pointed to the autonomy of areas and districts to set local policies by their own group conscience, and suggested continuing the conversation at local A.A. events and Regional Forums and in area discussions about possible future language-based and virtual areas. The committee report does not take up the proposal's second question, about where a past delegate who has moved may stand for trustee.

forwarded_items.title: Review the personal stories in the pamphlet on medications and other drugs (P-11)
forwarded_items.outcome: Advisory Action on the P-11 pamphlet, the subject of this item and of proposed agenda item 56. The trustees' Literature Committee forwarded it; under the Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) plan the P-11 item was on the agenda of the Conference Committee on Corrections. The Conference asked that 'The A.A. Member — Medications and Other Drugs' (P-11) be revised, with a progress report or draft pamphlet due at the 2027 Conference. The committee suggested updates that reflect today's medications and drugs and a more inclusive, representative range of A.A. recovery stories, keeping in mind that the pamphlet is meant for both alcoholics and the professionals A.A. works with.

forwarded_items.title: Revise and expand the pamphlet on medications and other drugs (P-11)
forwarded_items.outcome: Advisory Action on the P-11 pamphlet, the subject of this item and of proposed agenda item 50. The trustees' Literature Committee forwarded it; under the Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) plan the P-11 item was heard by the Conference Committee on Corrections. The Conference asked that P-11 be revised, with a progress report or draft pamphlet due at the 2027 Conference; the committee's suggestions covered current medications and drugs and a broader range of members' stories.

forwarded_items.title: A service piece or workbook-style study guide for the Twelve Steps

In the general sessions, a floor action asking the Conference to consider a Twelve Step study guide or workbook was declined to consider.
forwarded_items.cite: 2026 Final Report p. 103 (forwarded); p. 45 (committee consideration); p. 42 (floor action)

forwarded_items.title: Short stand-alone clips of professionals recommending A.A., made alongside any new videos for professionals

The trustees' CPC/Treatment and Accessibilities Committee forwarded it to the Conference Committee on Cooperation with the Professional Community (CPC), which agreed that short-form content is needed, noted that the office is already moving in that direction, and encouraged continued development of short outreach material.

forwarded_items.title: Adapt a district's animated videos of the safety flyer and the group safety card for A.A. World Services use

forwarded_items.outcome: No action on adapting the local videos; a new video was requested instead. World Services (AAWS) to create a new safety video from existing safety service material as budget permits (committee consideration).

notes.text: The February 2026 status grid lists every proposed agenda item (PAI) received for the 76th General Service Conference (held April 26 to May 2, 2026) and where each stood after the first-quarter board weekend of 2026. The General Service Office (GSO) sends this grid to Conference members each quarter under a 2025 Advisory Action that reaffirmed a 2016 request; in this cycle it went out on August 20 and November 22, 2025 and February 6, 2026, and motions are quoted exactly as they were submitted.
notes.cite: 2026 Final Report pp. 2, 84-85; Advisory Actions p770 (2025) and p694 (2016)

notes.text: How a proposal travels: it goes to the General Service Office (GSO) staff member serving as Conference coordinator; the staff suggest a disposition, study it in the light of past Conference actions and pass it to the appropriate trustees' committee. That committee may refer it to a Conference committee and usually decides how to present it (as a proposal, a presentation or workshop subject, or a committee concern). A Conference committee recommendation that the whole Conference approves with substantial unanimity (a two-thirds majority) after full floor discussion becomes an Advisory Action.
notes.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 pp. 42-43; Appendix U, p. 171

notes.text: 'Not forwarded to Conference' means the trustees' committee or board that reviewed the item did not place it on the 76th Conference agenda. Most trustees' committees' reports in the 2026 Final Report list each such item with a short reason; the trustees' General Service Conference Committee's report lists only the four items it forwarded. Topics that belong to the General Service Board, A.A. World Services (AAWS) or AA Grapevine are routed to that board; on this grid the three boards held 35 of the 110 items and forwarded none, and their reports in the Final Report do not list these items one by one. The trustees' committees forwarded 14 of their 73.
notes.cite: February 2026 PAI status grid; 2026 Final Report pp. 87-89, 104

notes.text: A common reason for not forwarding was that related work was already under way: a revision of Living Sober (proposed agenda item, or PAI, 53 asked for a chapter on anxiety and depression), other safety publications in development (PAI 23, safety questions for the group inventory, with a suggestion to resubmit later), new shared experience on social media being added to the pamphlet 'Understanding Anonymity' (P-47) (PAI 25, adding 'and social media' to Tradition Eleven), another short public service announcement (PSA) already in progress (PAI 51), and updates to self-support service material (PAI 100, a new section on contributions in 'The A.A. Group').

Another reason was that a past Conference had already considered the matter. For restoring earlier wording in Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions (proposed agenda items, or PAIs, 16 and 101), the trustees said the topic had been discussed at a prior Conference and no new information was offered; the 2021 Conference had revised passages on pages 66 and 117. For returning the Lord's Prayer to the closing options at International Convention Big Meetings (PAIs 6 and 29), the trustees called reconsideration premature, since a 2024 Advisory Action set six closing options that were used at the 2025 Convention. Earlier Conference discussion was also among the reasons given for PSAs on cable TV and streaming networks (PAI 38) and for using 'trusted servant' consistently in 'The A.A. Group' (PAI 48).
notes.cite: 2026 Final Report pp. 97, 105, 107, 115; Advisory Actions p3071 and p3076 (2021), p2282 (2024)

notes.text: Plain Language Big Book proposals were held over by design: a 2025 Advisory Action asked that proposals to rescind or revise the Plain Language Big Book be collected and deferred to the 77th Conference (2027), giving the Fellowship wider experience with the book. The trustees' Literature Committee cited it for proposed agenda items (PAIs) 7, 58, 86 and 108, and PAIs 7, 86 and 108 now appear in the deferred section of the October 2026 grid for the 77th Conference. PAI 60 was not forwarded because a subcommittee, set up under a second 2025 Advisory Action, was already designing the process for proposed changes; on PAI 43 (that the translator for that process be an A.A. member) the committee noted that Conference members review and approve all changes and that Concept XI calls for the best possible consultants.
notes.cite: 2026 Final Report pp. 101, 104-107; Advisory Actions p3128 and p3129 (2025); October 2026 PAI grid p. 37

notes.text: Some items were not forwarded because the trustees suggested wider consultation first or saw no widely expressed need: a pamphlet for Jewish members (proposed agenda item, or PAI, 1: broad consultation is often useful, so the trustees suggested sharing the idea in the district or area before any future proposal), a pamphlet on long-term sobriety (PAI 54: wider consultation would show whether the need is widely expressed), changes to the Anonymity Statement card (PAI 37: could benefit from wider group conscience at the district and area level), and a narrowly focused change to 'Questions and Answers on Sponsorship' (PAI 96: no widely expressed need; a broader review could be proposed instead). For the requests to stop publishing or to retire certain pamphlets (PAIs 15 and 36), the trustees noted that each pamphlet had been approved with substantial unanimity and saw no widely expressed need to eliminate them. For a pamphlet for neurodivergent alcoholics (PAI 87), the trustees said more exploration was needed and suggested the subject as a future Conference workshop topic.

Some were judged outside the Conference's decision or limited by law: service material such as the blue card (F-17, proposed agenda item, or PAI, 67) is the responsibility of A.A. World Services (AAWS) and General Service Office (GSO) staff; appointing the board's officers is the General Service Board's own responsibility under its bylaws (PAI 3 asked to drop the rule that the treasurer be a nonalcoholic, or Class A, trustee); the request for more detailed financial reports (PAI 11) was seen as raising confidentiality concerns and as outside the Conference's scope; and the trustees' Finance and Budgetary Committee said the Reserve Fund policies in PAIs 73 and 74 could keep the board from meeting its legal responsibilities, and preferred a broader Conference session on rebuilding the Reserve Fund.

'Not forwarded' was not always the end. Several items went to a working body instead: the three Spanish plain-language requests (proposed agenda items, or PAIs, 4, 71 and 106) to the subcommittee studying plain-language tools in Spanish; four Big Book suggestions (PAIs 8, 13, 14 and 98) to the Fifth Edition Big Book Subcommittee; the treasurer question (PAI 3) to the Preparing for Future Vacancies Subcommittee; and a sponsorship-pamphlet suggestion (PAI 62) to the Publishing Department for the next update. The trustees' Literature Committee also sent two anonymity items (PAIs 25 and 37) to the trustees' Public Information Committee, which took no action on them.

Forwarding is not approval. Of the 14 forwarded items, four (proposed agenda items 50 and 56 on the medications pamphlet P-11, and 103 and 104 on animated Steps and Traditions videos) led to three Advisory Actions. None of the other ten became an Advisory Action: nine were recorded as no action, and the Conference-location study (item 22) ended with a request for a progress report; several came with suggestions recorded as committee considerations. A Conference committee can take an item as it is, change it, take no action and explain why, or add considerations, and a recommendation needs substantial unanimity (a two-thirds majority) to become an Advisory Action.
notes.cite: 2026 Final Report pp. 39-53; Service Manual 2026-2028 pp. 42, 45

notes.text: Under the 2025-2026 Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) plan, new agenda items were spread across Conference committees, so several of these proposals were heard outside their usual committee: the P-11 pamphlet by Corrections, the Step study guide and the Conference-location study by Finance, area service eligibility by Archives, the safety videos by Treatment and Accessibilities, and the Steps and Traditions videos by Trustees. The 76th Conference voted to end the EDW process after the 78th Conference (2028).
notes.cite: 2026 Final Report pp. 39-41, 44-46, 53, 86; Advisory Action p3718

notes.text: An item that is not on the agenda, or that a committee did not move forward, can still be raised by a Conference member in the general sessions as a floor action. Its maker states the reasons, and the Conference may vote by two-thirds to decline to consider it. In 2026 a floor action asking for a Twelve Step study guide or workbook, the subject of proposed agenda item 70, was declined to consider.
notes.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 pp. 42, 49, 174-175; 2026 Final Report p. 42

notes.text: Items can be submitted again. The trustees sometimes invited a later or broader resubmission (proposed agenda items 1, 23 and 96). The last items on this grid arrived on September 30, 2025. A 2024 Advisory Action moved the deadline for the 2025 Conference to no earlier than September 30, 2024, and the trustees' General Service Conference Committee then set September 30 as the deadline, with later submissions considered for the following year. The 2026 Conference's Inventory Implementation committee asked that Conference members tell the Fellowship more clearly that the cutoff applies only to the next Conference and that proposals are welcome all year; this was among the recommendations committed to the General Service Board, not an Advisory Action.
notes.cite: February 2026 PAI status grid; Advisory Action p3707 (2024); 2025 Final Report p. 86; 2026 Final Report pp. 42, 104-107

notes.text: What changed for the next cycle: from October 2026 the incoming Conference committee chairs attend the fall (fourth-quarter) board weekend instead of the January one, giving them a longer window to comment on proposed agenda items (PAIs) while the trustees' committees review them. The Inventory Implementation recommendations committed to the board also proposed replacing the October feedback call with a joint meeting of trustees' and Conference committees, all members with voice and vote, to decide what happens to each PAI, and keeping items on the status grid until they are resolved.

Founders' writings: the General Service Board received three requests to define founders' writings (proposed agenda items 17, 94 and 97) and forwarded none. Separately, a 2025 Advisory Action asked the board to sort A.A. World Services and AA Grapevine literature written before 1971 into Recovery, Service or Archival/Historical. At the 2026 Conference the Report and Charter committee noted that there is no formal definition of 'founders' (the term 'cofounders' usually means Bill W. and Dr. Bob) and asked that the classification topic go to the trustees' Literature Committee for more input.
notes.cite: February 2026 PAI status grid; 2026 Final Report p. 52; Advisory Action p4819 (2025)

notes.text: Trends in this cycle: requests about literature other than the Big Book text were the largest group (27 of 110) and supplied 5 of the 14 forwarded items; proposals about boards, offices and the Conference itself (16) and about safety and inclusion (11) came next. No item about founders' writings (4, counting a request to label some pamphlets 'Foundational Material'), specific Big Book or Twelve and Twelve wording (5) or the Plain Language Big Book (6) was forwarded. No item in this cycle fell under Charter protection for the Big Book, a review period before Big Book changes, or floor-action procedure; all three topics appear on the October 2026 grid for the 77th Conference (for example items 10, 167 and 39).
notes.cite: February 2026 PAI status grid (primary themes assigned for this summary); October 2026 PAI grid items 10, 39, 167

notes.text: How this summary counts: the February 2026 grid has 110 rows: 14 forwarded, 94 not forwarded and 2 withdrawn (proposed agenda item 18, a duplicate removed in favor of item 36, and item 64, replaced by item 87). Each item is given one primary theme; the two withdrawn rows are counted under the theme of the item that replaced them. The committee shown for each forwarded item is the Conference committee that actually heard it.

history.public_note: aa.org does not post the status grid. Its public 'Proposed Agenda Item Information' page (read October 24, 2026) says an individual A.A. member can submit a proposed agenda item (PAI), and that groups, districts and areas can get help from their general service representative (GSR), district, area committee or delegate. For the form it says to contact the area delegate or the Conference desk at the General Service Office (GSO). It gives the 77th Conference deadline of September 30, 2026, 11:59 pm, says later submissions will be considered for the 2028 Conference, and says that after the trustees' committee or board meets, the committee secretary will tell the submitter the outcome. It has no link to a grid or list of submissions. The grid goes to Conference members (2026 Final Report p. 84, PDF p. 85): the area delegates, trustees, nontrustee directors and A.A. staff who make up the Conference (Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 41). Since 2008 GSO staff have kept the grid on the Conference Dashboard, a password-protected site for Conference members (2018 Final Report p. 28, PDF p. 29; 2019 Final Report p. 21, PDF p. 22; Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 33, p. 35); GSO now sends Conference material through its OnBoard platform (2026 Final Report p. 88, PDF p. 89). Since a 2025 Advisory Action (p770), GSO sends the grid every quarter. For the 76th cycle it went out on August 20, 2025, November 22, 2025 and February 6, 2026 (2026 Final Report p. 84, PDF p. 85). The trustees' General Service Conference Committee named Conference members as the audience for these status reports, with members passing the information on to their regions and areas (2024 Final Report pp. 70-71, PDF pp. 71-72). The grid's own header says the items listed are not the final agenda, and that the final list comes in early February (October 1, 2026 grid).
