process.text: Any A.A. member, group, district or area can start a proposal. The Service Manual suggests that a general service representative (GSR) first talk the idea over with the group, then at district or area meetings; a district or area can then send it on. Many agenda items travel from the group through the GSR, district and area. The manual's chart 'The Path for an Idea to Become an Agenda Item' shows the full route: idea, GSO Conference coordinator, trustees' committee, Conference committee, the full Conference, and the General Service Board.
process.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 22, p. 43, p. 171 (Appendix U)

process.text: Proposals go to the General Service Office (GSO) staff member serving as Conference coordinator, whose listed duties include receiving proposed agenda items (PAIs). aa.org says to get the form from the area delegate or the Conference desk. GSO's Conference staff suggest how to handle each item to the chair of the trustees' General Service Conference Committee and the Director of Staff Services, check the item against past Conference actions, and pass it on.
process.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 43; 2026 Final Report p. 88 (PDF p. 89); aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page (read October 24, 2026)

process.text: For the 77th Conference (April 11-17, 2027, New York) proposals had to arrive by September 30, 2026, 11:59 pm. Anything received later is held for the following Conference, the 78th in 2028. The cut-off only closes the list for the next Conference, and proposals can be sent at any time of year.
process.cite: aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page (read October 24, 2026); 2025 Final Report p. 85 (PDF p. 86); 2024 Final Report p. 51 (PDF p. 52); 2023 Final Report p. 43 (PDF p. 44)

process.text: Each item gets a number and goes to the trustees' committee or board whose work it touches, for discussion at its next meeting. Examples are the trustees' Literature Committee, the A.A. World Services (AAWS) board and the Grapevine board. The grid's 'Forwarded to' column names this reviewing body. At this stage 'Forwarded to' means sent to that body for review, not to the Conference. Items that belong to the General Service Board, AAWS or Grapevine are sent to those boards.
process.cite: October 1, 2026 and June 5, 2026 grids (header and columns); aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page; 2024 Final Report p. 71 (PDF p. 72)

process.text: GSO lists every proposal, quoted exactly as submitted, in a status grid for Conference members and sends an update every quarter. For the 76th cycle it went out on August 20, 2025, then on November 22, 2025 and February 6, 2026, each after a board weekend. For the 77th cycle, grids dated June 5, 2026 (8 items) and October 1, 2026 (221 items) are in hand.
process.cite: Advisory Action p770 (2025); 2026 Final Report p. 83 (PDF p. 84), p. 84 (PDF p. 85); June 5 and October 1, 2026 grids

process.text: Before the fall board weekend, trustees' committee chairs ask the members of the matching Conference committees whether proposals should go to the Conference. For example, the chair of the trustees' General Service Conference Committee met the Agenda, Policy/Admissions and Report and Charter committees in fall 2024, and the Agenda and Policy/Admissions committees in fall 2025, and brought their views into the trustees' decision on each item; the trustees' Nominating Committee heard the Conference Committee on Trustees the same way. This October call took the place of the call before the January board weekend once the Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) plan moved the deadline earlier; the Service Manual still describes the January call. From October 2026 the 77th Conference committee chairs also attend the fall board weekend instead of the January one, which gives them more time to comment on proposals.
process.cite: 2022 Final Report p. 33 (PDF p. 34); 2023 Final Report p. 66 (PDF p. 67); 2025 Final Report p. 84 (PDF p. 85); 2026 Final Report p. 49 (PDF p. 50), p. 86 (PDF p. 87), p. 108 (PDF p. 109); Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 49, p. 63

process.step: 7. Fall board weekend: the trustees decide
process.text: At the fall General Service Board (GSB) weekend the trustees' committees and boards decide each item. They can forward it to a Conference committee, keep it at board level for more background and study, or route it to the AAWS or Grapevine board. Similar proposals can be grouped into one agenda item. For the 77th cycle this weekend is October 30-November 2, 2026. After the meeting the committee secretary tells the submitter the outcome.
process.cite: October 1, 2026 grid (header); 2026 Final Report p. 102 (PDF p. 103); calendar.json gsb-q4-2026 (aa.org board calendar); aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page

process.text: After the fall board weekend, Conference members receive a preliminary agenda. It lists the proposals forwarded to the Conference, ongoing work, standing items, and new items from trustees' committees. An updated status grid follows; in 2025 it came out on November 22.
process.cite: 2024 Final Report p. 70 (PDF p. 71); 2026 Final Report p. 84 (PDF p. 85)

process.step: 9. Winter board weekend and final agenda (early February)
process.text: The final agenda comes out after the January (winter) board weekend. It includes the workload plan, which can place some items with a committee other than the one they were sent to. The grid header says the final list of Conference committee agenda items is available in early February. For the 77th Conference this weekend is January 29-February 1, 2027.
process.cite: 2024 Final Report p. 70 (PDF p. 71); October 1, 2026 grid (header); 2022 Final Report p. 4 (PDF p. 5); calendar.json gsb-q1-2027 (aa.org board calendar)

process.text: Background on every agenda item goes to Conference members in English, French and Spanish at the same time and is shared through the Fellowship to inform discussion. In 2026 it was scheduled to go out February 17-20. One to two weeks after that, Conference members get a list of the proposals not forwarded, with a reason for each.
process.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 45; Advisory Action p3692 (2022); 2026 Final Report p. 83 (PDF p. 84); 2024 Final Report p. 70 (PDF p. 71); 2025 Final Report p. 89 (PDF p. 90)

process.text: Once background is out and before the April Conference, areas, districts and groups study the agenda and, through local pre-Conference sessions, tell their delegate their group conscience. The Service Manual calls the area assembly a vital part of the communication process from the group to the Conference.
process.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 22, p. 33

process.text: Most agenda items go to one of the 13 standing Conference committees. These meet early in the week, and most also hold a joint session with their trustees' committee at the start of the week, which is for sharing information only, with no actions taken. A committee can take an item as written, change it, take up new items, or take no action (usually saying why). It can also add 'additional committee considerations' or send an item back to a trustees' committee for a later Conference.
process.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 45

process.text: Each committee reports its recommendations to the full Conference. A recommendation becomes an Advisory Action only with substantial unanimity, meaning a two-thirds vote. One that wins a simple majority but falls short is recorded in the Final Report for information. Delegates can also bring forward an item that did not leave committee, or was never on the agenda, as a floor action. The body first votes on whether to consider it.
process.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 42, p. 43, p. 49

process.text: The General Service Board votes to affirm the Advisory Actions and sends each one to the right trustees' committee, to GSO or to a corporate board to carry out. Each delegate reports the outcome to their area, and each GSR tells their group.
process.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 5, p. 43

process.text: The item has been received and assigned to a trustees' committee or board, which has not decided yet. In the 77th-cycle grids every active item has this status, because the trustees take up these items at the fall 2026 board weekend. It does not mean the item is on the Conference agenda.
process.cite: June 5, 2026 and October 1, 2026 grids; calendar.json gsb-q4-2026

process.text: The reviewing trustees' committee or board sent the item to a Conference committee, so it appears on the Conference agenda. It may be grouped with similar items, or placed with another committee under the workload plan. Forwarding is not approval: the Conference committee and then the full Conference decide. In the February 2026 grid for the 76th Conference, 14 of 110 items had this status.
process.cite: February 2026 grid (counted); 2026 Final Report p. 102 (PDF p. 103); 2022 Final Report p. 4 (PDF p. 5); Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 45

process.text: The reviewing body did not place the item on the Conference agenda. It may be kept at board level for more background, handled by the A.A. World Services (AAWS) or Grapevine board, or closed because the committee took no action to forward it. The submitter is told the outcome and can submit again in a later year. Trustees' committees sometimes suggest resubmitting once related work is finished.
process.cite: October 1, 2026 grid (header); 2024 Final Report p. 71 (PDF p. 72); 2023 Final Report p. 67 (PDF p. 68); 2026 Final Report p. 103 (PDF p. 104), p. 104 (PDF p. 105); aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page

process.text: 'Superseded by PAI' followed by a number means a later item replaced this one, and the grid names the newer item. In the 76th-cycle grid, one item was withdrawn with the submitter's permission in favor of a later one, and a duplicate was removed the same way. Other entries read 'Removed with submitter approval' or 'Withdrawn, no requested action'. One entry says it was removed as a human resources matter not suitable for wider distribution, and another that it brought no relevant Conference or committee action. The October 1, 2026 grid lists 11 such entries in its 'Withdrawn / Superseded' section, and they still count toward its 221 items.
process.cite: October 1, 2026 grid ('Withdrawn / Superseded' section); February 2026 grid (items 18 and 64)

process.step: Deferred Plain Language Big Book proposals
process.text: The October 2026 grid has a separate section with three proposals from the 2025 cycle that ask the Conference to reconsider the approval of the Plain Language Big Book, to discontinue it, or to retire and replace it. The February 2026 grid shows them as 'Not forwarded'. The trustees' Literature Committee took no action on them because a 2025 Advisory Action asked that proposals to withdraw or revise the book be collected and held until the 77th Conference (2027), so the Fellowship could gain wider experience with it. A companion 2025 action asked for a trustees' Literature Committee process to receive, assess and forward proposed changes to the Plain Language Big Book.
process.cite: October 1, 2026 grid (deferred section); February 2026 grid (items 7, 86, 108); 2026 Final Report p. 103 (PDF p. 104), p. 105 (PDF p. 106); Advisory Actions p3128, p3129 (2025)

process.step: What happens to items not forwarded
process.text: The committee secretary contacts the submitter with the outcome. Conference members receive a list of the items not forwarded, with a reason for each, shortly after background goes out; in 2019 the Policy/Admissions committee noted that the grid itself carried a reason for each item not forwarded. The submitter can send the item again for a later Conference. During Conference week a committee can take up new items, and a delegate can raise a topic as a floor action.
process.cite: aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page; 2024 Final Report p. 70 (PDF p. 71); 2019 Final Report p. 39 (PDF p. 40); 2023 Final Report p. 67 (PDF p. 68); Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 45, p. 49

facts.text: Who may submit: the Service Manual names individual A.A. members, groups, delegates, area assemblies, area committee members, trustees, and directors and staff of A.A. World Services and the Grapevine as sources of Conference agenda items. aa.org says an individual member can submit a proposed agenda item (PAI), and that groups, districts and areas can get help from their general service representative (GSR), district, area committee or delegate.
facts.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 43, p. 91; aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page (read October 24, 2026)

facts.text: What fits the Conference: the Service Manual says Conference action is meant for proposals important to A.A.'s future, policy decisions, requests to change Conference-approved literature, and matters that may need the collective conscience of the Fellowship. Suggestions that are not about overall policy go to the most suitable part of the service structure.
facts.cite: Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 43, p. 44

facts.text: In 2023 the Conference Committee on Policy/Admissions asked the trustees' General Service Conference Committee to consider a short video or other message making two points. First, a proposed agenda item (PAI) can be sent at any time of year. Second, it is meant to record the outcome of a group conscience, not to act as a petition or suggestion box. No video was made; instead the introduction of the form was updated to carry these points.
facts.cite: 2023 Final Report p. 43 (PDF p. 44); 2024 Final Report p. 68 (PDF p. 69)

facts.text: The trustees' General Service Conference Committee chose to keep sending the proposed agenda item form to areas through Conference members, and the General Service Office (GSO) provides it on request. The committee had raised the concern that wide online distribution might lead members to bypass their assemblies and service structure. The updated form describes the Conference as a year-round effort and encourages taking part through the local area structure.
facts.cite: 2024 Final Report p. 68 (PDF p. 69); 2025 Final Report p. 89 (PDF p. 90)

facts.text: Deadline history, early years: in 1963 subjects were to reach the Agenda Committee throughout the year. In 1993 items were due by January 15, with final agendas and committee background sent by February 15. In 2013 the deadline moved from January 15 to December 15, starting in December 2014 for the 65th Conference.

Deadline history, recent years: the Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) plan moved the deadline to September 15, first for the 2022 Conference. A 2024 Advisory Action moved it to no earlier than September 30, 2024, for the 2025 Conference. The trustees' General Service Conference Committee then chose September 30, after finding that coordination and cost made it a better fit than two possible October dates. For the 77th Conference the deadline was September 30, 2026, 11:59 pm.
facts.cite: 2020 Final Report p. 22 (PDF p. 23); 2022 Final Report p. 32 (PDF p. 33); Advisory Action p3707 (2024); 2025 Final Report p. 85 (PDF p. 86); aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page

facts.text: Late items roll forward to the next Conference. A 1963 action asked that items not included on the current agenda be offered to the following year's committee. In 2024 the Conference Committee on Trustees affirmed that proposals received after the deadline are processed the following year, and the Policy/Admissions committee asked that the form say so; in 2025 the trustees' General Service Conference Committee noted that it does. aa.org says submissions after September 30, 2026 will be considered for the 2028 Conference.
facts.cite: Advisory Action p32 (1963); 2024 Final Report p. 45 (PDF p. 46), p. 51 (PDF p. 52); 2025 Final Report p. 85 (PDF p. 86); aa.org Proposed Agenda Item Information page

facts.text: The grids fit this pattern. The earliest date received in the 77th-cycle grid is January 30, 2026, and in the 76th-cycle grid it is February 17, 2025. Both dates fall after the previous year's September 30 deadline.
facts.cite: October 1, 2026 grid and February 2026 grid, Date Received column

facts.text: Most proposals arrive close to the deadline. Of the 221 items in the October 1, 2026 grid, 156 are dated September 2026: 74 in the last week (September 24-30) and 32 on September 30 itself. In the 76th-cycle grid, 79 of 110 are dated September 2025, 35 of them in the last week. Two items in each grid have no date.
facts.cite: October 1, 2026 grid and February 2026 grid, Date Received column (counted)

facts.text: The 77th-cycle list grew from 8 items in the grid dated June 5, 2026 to 221 items in the grid dated October 1, 2026.
facts.cite: June 5, 2026 grid header; October 1, 2026 grid header

facts.text: Reviewing bodies for the 221 items in the October 1, 2026 grid: trustees' General Service Conference Committee 96, trustees' Literature Committee 61, A.A. World Services (AAWS) board 17, Grapevine board 11, trustees' Finance and Budgetary Committee 7, trustees' Public Information Committee 6, General Service Board 4, trustees' Nominating Committee 3, trustees' International Conventions/Regional Forums Committee 3, trustees' Cooperation with the Professional Community/Treatment and Accessibilities Committee 1, and trustees' Corrections Committee 1. Another 11 are withdrawn, superseded or removed.

facts.text: Outcomes by reviewing body in the February 2026 grid for the 76th Conference: 14 of 110 items were forwarded. That was 8 of 39 reviewed by the trustees' Literature Committee, 4 of 16 by the trustees' General Service Conference Committee, 1 of 3 by the trustees' Cooperation with the Professional Community/Treatment and Accessibilities Committee, and 1 of 4 by the trustees' Finance and Budgetary Committee. No item reviewed by the A.A. World Services (AAWS) board (20), the General Service Board (11), the Grapevine board (4), or the trustees' Public Information (4), Nominating (4) or International Conventions/Regional Forums (3) committees was marked forwarded. The other 2 items were removed.

facts.text: Trustees' committees can group similar proposals. In the 76th cycle the trustees' Literature Committee forwarded three safety-related proposals and recommended grouping them into one agenda item.
facts.cite: 2026 Final Report p. 102 (PDF p. 103)

facts.text: Status grid history: General Service Office (GSO) staff have kept a grid of all proposals since 2008. It is posted on the Conference Dashboard, the password-protected site for Conference members, and updated as items move through the trustees' committees. A 2016 Advisory Action asked GSO to post the status of proposed agenda items on the dashboard and keep it current. In 2017 the Conference Agenda Committee asked that the grid show each trustees' committee decision and be posted soon after the January board weekend. From at least 2018 to 2020 the grid was posted in English, French and Spanish.
facts.cite: 2018 Final Report p. 28 (PDF p. 29), p. 77 (PDF p. 78); 2019 Final Report p. 21 (PDF p. 22), p. 69 (PDF p. 70); Advisory Action p694 (2016); 2017 Final Report p. 80 (PDF p. 81); 2020 Final Report p. 22 (PDF p. 23); Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 33, p. 35

facts.text: A 2025 Advisory Action reaffirmed the 2016 action and asked the General Service Office (GSO) to provide a grid of proposed agenda items and their status every quarter. The trustees' General Service Conference Committee previewed the draft and asked that every motion be put in quotation marks, to show that each one is reported exactly as submitted. Each grid page notes that motions appear in their original language and are translated to reflect the submitter's intent as clearly as possible.
facts.cite: Advisory Action p770 (2025); 2025 Final Report p. 36 (PDF p. 37); 2026 Final Report p. 83 (PDF p. 84); October 1, 2026 grid footnote

facts.text: A 2017 floor action to place the submission letters for proposed agenda items on the Conference dashboard was not approved.
facts.cite: 2017 Final Report p. 83 (PDF p. 84)

facts.text: A 2016 floor action asked the General Service Board to develop a policy giving area delegates a role in vetting and selecting proposed agenda items. The trustees' plan in response suggested a call, before the January board weekend, between each Conference committee and its trustees' committee chair to review submitted items. The 2018 Conference Agenda Committee noted this had not yet happened and asked for the calls to start in January 2019, and they were held that year.
facts.cite: Advisory Action p695 (2016); 2017 Final Report p. 42 (PDF p. 43); 2018 Final Report p. 49 (PDF p. 50); 2019 Final Report p. 21 (PDF p. 22)

facts.text: Earlier Conferences also tried to give areas more time. A 1974 action suggested settling as many agenda items as possible at the October board meetings so that the November Quarterly Report could start early assembly discussion. A 1986 action, citing the growing number of topics, asked delegates to encourage members to bring their concerns to district meetings and area assemblies, and the committee also suggested sending items to the coordinator early. A 1992 action asked that committee members learn of new items as soon as practical rather than waiting until January.

The Equitable Distribution of Workload (EDW) process balances committee workloads by moving some agenda items to committees other than the one they were submitted to. It began as a three-year trial for the 72nd Conference (2022) and was adopted in 2024. A 2026 Advisory Action ends it after the 78th Conference (2028).
facts.cite: Advisory Actions p3679 (2021), p3706 (2024), p3718 (2026); 2022 Final Report p. 4 (PDF p. 5)

facts.text: The 77th Conference committee chairs attend the October 2026 (fourth-quarter) board weekend instead of the January 2027 one, which gives them longer to comment on proposals under review. The trustees described this as restoring an earlier practice of having the chairs present when proposals are considered. The 2026-2028 Service Manual still describes the January visit.
facts.cite: 2026 Final Report p. 49 (PDF p. 50), p. 85 (PDF p. 86); Service Manual 2026-2028 p. 45, p. 63

facts.text: At the 2026 Conference, a set of Inventory Implementation recommendations was committed (referred) to the General Service Board instead of being voted on as Advisory Actions. They included: Conference committees seeing every proposal as it arrives through the quarterly grid; keeping the grid as a living list until each item is resolved; telling the Fellowship that the deadline applies only to the next Conference and that year-round submissions are encouraged; replacing the October feedback call with a joint meeting of trustees' and Conference committees, all members having voice and vote on what goes to the next Conference; and recognizing that Conference committees may bring forward items not on their agenda or defer an item to a future Conference.
facts.cite: 2026 Final Report p. 41 (PDF p. 42)

facts.text: Also at the 2026 Conference, the Policy/Admissions committee recommended that the board plan a nine-member working group (six area delegates, two board members and one General Service Office staff member) to improve how proposals are selected for Conference committees. The recommendation was presented but did not reach the two-thirds vote needed.
facts.cite: 2026 Final Report p. 40 (PDF p. 41), p. 41 (PDF p. 42)

facts.text: The 2025 Conference inventory asked whether the way proposals are submitted and selected leads the Conference to address the Fellowship's most widely expressed needs. Its summary recorded strong agreement that the current process draws complaints more than solutions, and a suggestion to reword the form to ask how a proposal helps carry the message. It also recorded delegates' sense of being left out when the list is narrowed, reply letters to proposals not forwarded being seen as inadequate and formulaic, and the idea of a two-year agenda cycle. Proposals that came out of the inventory included ending deadlines in favor of year-round submission and better feedback on proposals not forwarded.
facts.cite: 2025 Final Report p. 32 (PDF p. 33), p. 35 (PDF p. 36)

facts.text: The 2025 Conference Committee on Trustees discussed how proposed agenda items reach the final agenda and said it strongly agrees that the Fellowship, through its delegates, should have more voice in the final decision.
facts.cite: 2025 Final Report p. 52 (PDF p. 53)

facts.text: A 2025 floor action to cut the number of standing agenda items, to leave more room for proposals from the Fellowship, was declined for consideration.
facts.cite: 2025 Final Report p. 53 (PDF p. 54), p. 54 (PDF p. 55)

facts.text: A 2024 floor action proposed that proposals asking for censure or reorganization have no deadline and go straight to the Conference Committee on Trustees; it was not approved. In 2025-2026 a trustees' Nominating Committee subcommittee studied a recommitted 2025 recommendation of the same kind. It raised concerns that sending such proposals directly to a Conference committee could bypass the General Service Board's role under the Conference Charter and might not protect the submitter's confidentiality. A 2026 Advisory Action asked the board to form an ad hoc committee, made up like the Conference, to document how motions to censure or reorganize are received, considered and forwarded, with a report to the 2027 Conference Committee on Trustees.
facts.cite: 2024 Final Report p. 51 (PDF p. 52); 2026 Final Report p. 40 (PDF p. 41), p. 108 (PDF p. 109); Advisory Action p5635 (2026)

facts.text: For scale, the whole Conference agenda, including standing and ongoing items and not only proposals, has run from about 70 to about 110 items. It averaged 72.5 items before 2017, then held 108 in 2017, 91 in 2018, more than 86 in 2023, more than 88 in 2024, and 70 at the 2026 Conference. The 2025 Final Report notes that the number of proposed agenda items affects the Conference's workload.
facts.cite: 2019 Final Report p. 13 (PDF p. 14); 2023 Final Report p. 3 (PDF p. 4); 2024 Final Report p. 3 (PDF p. 4); 2026 Final Report p. 3 (PDF p. 4); 2025 Final Report p. 10 (PDF p. 11)

facts.text: Background languages: a 2017 floor action set a goal, starting in 2018, of sending background in English by February 15 and in Spanish and French by the first week of March. A 2022 Advisory Action has all background released in the three languages at the same time.
facts.cite: Advisory Actions p704 (2017), p3692 (2022)

facts.text: The Plain Language Big Book: A Tool for Reading Alcoholics Anonymous was approved by a 2024 Advisory Action. In 2025 the Conference decided that proposals to withdraw or revise it be gathered and held until the 77th Conference in 2027.
facts.cite: Advisory Actions p3121 (2024), p3128 (2025)

facts.text: The 77th General Service Conference meets April 11-17, 2027, at the New York Marriott Marquis.
facts.cite: 2025 Final Report p. 45 (PDF p. 46), p. 85 (PDF p. 86)
